title: Unlist the create_issue MCP tool superseded by save_work_item
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

The GitLab MCP server advertises its tool catalog via `tools/list`. At GA, that advertised catalog becomes a compatibility contract, so tools that have been superseded need to stop being advertised before GA. This MR marks the REST-backed `create_issue` MCP tool as unlisted, since it is superseded by the `save_work_item` MCP tool (work item creation already covers issue creation).

Unlisting hides the tool from `tools/list` and from the AI Catalog tool picker, but it stays fully callable through `tools/call`, so existing callers keep working while they migrate to `save_work_item`.

Changes:

- `route_setting :mcp, ..., unlisted: true` added to `create_issue` in `lib/api/issues.rb`.
- Docs updated in `doc/user/model_context_protocol/mcp_server_tools.md` with an "Unlisted in GitLab 19.4" history entry and a supersession note pointing to `save_work_item`.
- CE and EE `list_tools` specs updated to remove `create_issue` from expected annotations, with header-filter fixtures swapped to `get_pipeline`.
- Added a context asserting retired tools are not advertised but remain resolvable through `Mcp::Tools::Manager#get_tool`.

## References

- Retirement umbrella: [Retire superseded MCP tools before GA](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/622712)
- Closes [Unlist create_issue MCP tool](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/625129)

## How to verify locally

- `bundle exec rubocop` clean.
- CE `list_tools` spec: 23 examples green. EE `list_tools` spec: 4 examples green. `call_tool` create_issue spec: green.
- GDK e2e over real HTTP JSON-RPC (`POST /api/v4/mcp`): `tools/list` no longer contains `create_issue`; `tools/call create_issue` still created a real issue.

The change bumps the `graphql` gem from 2.5.11 to 2.6.10 and adds `config/initializers/graphql_subscriptions_serialize_patch.rb`, which carries two unreleased upstream fixes to `GraphQL::Subscriptions::Serialize` — the serializer that round-trips user-controlled subscription arguments through ActionCable/Redis.

19.0 sits outside the original three-version backport window, so it was raised separately with release management. 19.1, 19.2 and 19.3 already carry the fix; 18.11 is being backported alongside this MR.

### Why the gem bump comes with it

The initializer is pinned to graphql 2.6.10 by an explicit version guard, and the third upstream fix it depends on (restricting timestamp deserialization) ships in the gem at 2.6.8 — it exists in no 2.5.x release, as that series ended at 2.5.26. Backporting the initializer alone would mean rewriting it and hand-maintaining a second copy of a security patch, so the gem moves with it and the commit applies as-is.

### Risk

The 2.5 → 2.6 minor needed no application changes on the default branch: [`1d82305f`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/commit/1d82305fd8760bd262a15e038fa0749a32a2b7c3) ("Upgrade GraphQL to 2.6.3") touched only the Gemfile, lockfiles and the two introspection fixtures. The breaking changes in the range don't apply here: `Schema::Visibility` is unused in the codebase, and none of our tracers hook `execute_query_lazy`. Gem metadata is unchanged — same runtime dependencies, same `required_ruby_version`.

### Regenerated, not cherry-picked

* `Gemfile.lock`, `Gemfile.next.lock`, `Gemfile.checksum`, `Gemfile.next.checksum` (via `bundle install` + `bundler:gemfile:sync`)
* `public/-/graphql/introspection_result.json` and `introspection_result_no_deprecated.json` (via `gitlab:graphql:generate_all_introspection_schemas`) — a `VARIABLE_DEFINITION` directive-location reordering, identical to what `1d82305f` produced on master

title: Silence vscode-languageserver UMD critical-dependency warnings
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Upon installing and starting the [GDK](https://gitlab-org.gitlab.io/gitlab-development-kit/) we are greeted with the below screen when loading via localhost:3000 for the first time, this address #600161 , the issue was narrowed down to warning for the vscode language server originating form the webpack.config.js.  

![image.png](/uploads/837b3f7aa5bf5bb97c9ceb91ec428e83/image.png){width=661 height=600}

## The problem

When you start GDK, two warnings pop up in the browser overlay:

`Critical dependency: require function is used in a way in which
dependencies cannot be statically extracted
`

…coming from `vscode-languageserver-types` and `vscode-languageserver-textdocument`.

## Why it happens

These two packages each ship **two versions** of their code in `node_modules`:

1. **UMD version** (`lib/umd/main.js`) — old format that works in Node.js, browsers, and AMD loaders. It contains code like `if (typeof require === "function") require(...)` to detect its environment.
2. **ESM version** (`lib/esm/main.js`) — modern ES modules. Clean `import`/`export` syntax, no tricks.

The package's `package.json` tells bundlers which one to use:

`"main": "./lib/umd/main.js",        ← old field, points to UMD
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./lib/esm/main.js",  ← modern field, points to ESM
    "browser": "./lib/esm/main.js",
    "default": "./lib/umd/main.js"
  }
}
`

**The catch:** GitLab still uses webpack 4, which doesn't understand the `exports` field. So webpack falls back to `main` and pulls in the UMD version. Webpack then sees the dynamic `require(...)` call inside it, can't figure out at build time what's being required, and prints the warning.

## The fix

Tell webpack directly: "When anyone imports these packages, give them the ESM file." That's what a webpack `alias` does — it's a redirect.

In [config/webpack.config.js](vscode-webview://1j8h2fu1c39r35acka0iljmuhph3d3l9ufiaknl4ds8jgh9t34l0/config/webpack.config.js):

`'vscode-languageserver-types':
  '.../node_modules/vscode-languageserver-types/lib/esm/main.js',
'vscode-languageserver-textdocument':
  '.../node_modules/vscode-languageserver-textdocument/lib/esm/main.js',
`

Now webpack skips the UMD wrapper entirely and reads the clean ESM file. No dynamic `require`, no warning, overlay clean.

## How to set up and validate locally

1. Install and load the latest version of GDK as per https://gitlab-org.gitlab.io/gitlab-development-kit/
2. Load the GDK with localhost:3000 to experience the error
3. Apply this patch and run \`gdk stop && gdk start\`
4. Check and you should not see the overlay error any more.

title: Wire risk_severity into the rule-type picker and switchboard
description:
## What

Final slice of the risk_severity DFW rule builder work. Makes the new
rule type reachable:

- `rule_list.vue` reads the `dependency_firewall_risk_severity_rule`
  feature flag and passes the flag-gated item list into
  `rule_type_select.vue`'s new `items` prop.
- `rule_section.vue` renders `RiskSeverityRuleBuilder` for rules of
  type `risk_severity`.

With the flag off, behaviour is unchanged. With it on, **Risk
severity replaces Vulnerability** in the "Add new rule" dropdown —
this is a deliberate, mutually-exclusive swap, not an additive 5th
option, matching the direction agreed for this rollout.

## Screenshots or screen recordings

Verified live in a local GDK (on the proving branch, `poc-dfw-risk-severity-rule` / !253663, which contains this exact cumulative diff): flag on/off correctly swaps the dropdown option, adding/removing severity rows works, threshold values sanitize to non-negative integers, and the resulting policy YAML validates against the schema end-to-end via the real "Configure with a merge request" save flow.

## How to set up and validate locally

1. Enable the flags:
   ```
   Feature.enable(:dependency_firewall_phase1)
   Feature.enable(:dependency_firewall_phase2)
   Feature.enable(:dependency_firewall_risk_severity_rule)
   ```
2. Go to a project's Security > Policies > New policy > Dependency Firewall
3. Click "Add new rule" — "Risk severity" appears instead of "Vulnerability"
4. Add a rule, add a few severities with thresholds, save

## Review notes

Caught and fixed in review:

- `getAddRuleTypeItems` appended the risk_severity item to the end of
  the list instead of substituting it at vulnerability's original
  position, so the flag-on dropdown order didn't match the intended
  swap. Fixed to substitute in place.
- The default policy YAML's rule-hint comment hardcoded specific
  rule-type names ("license, vulnerability, or malicious"), which
  would go stale the moment the flag swaps one of them out. Made it
  generic.
- The "fully filled-in policy" schema test only covered three rule
  types; added risk_severity and fixed the test title.
- Added a comment on `getAddRuleTypeItems` naming the flag it depends
  on and what to do when the flag is removed, so the flag-cleanup pass
  doesn't miss it.

Also added test coverage that was missing even in the POC branch:
`rule_section.vue`'s new `risk_severity` branch and `rule_list.vue`'s
flag-gated dropdown were previously untested.

## MRs in this series

1. Feature flag definition + push (!253730)
2. Shared rule-type constants/utils (!253743)
3. New risk_severity rule builder component (!253750) — this MR is stacked on it
4. This MR — wiring into the rule-type picker and switchboard

None of these merge into each other; each targets its own branch and
is reviewed independently. `poc-dfw-risk-severity-rule` (!253663)
remains the reference branch proving the whole thing works end-to-end.

## Related

Relates to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/627719

title: Add group_filter LDAP configuration setting
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

This merge request implements a new optional `group_filter` LDAP configuration setting that allows administrators to narrow which LDAP entries are treated as groups during LDAP group sync operations. The feature mirrors the existing `user_filter` setting, accepting an RFC 4515 LDAP filter string that is ANDed with GitLab's existing group search filters to refine the group discovery process. This is useful when LDAP directory entries have non-standard objectClass definitions or naming conventions that differ from GitLab's defaults, or when the configured group_base contains non-group entries that need to be excluded. The configuration is defined in the CE layer (`lib/gitlab/auth/ldap/config.rb`) and integrated into EE's `Adapter#groups` and `#nested_groups` methods via a new private `group_filter` helper, following the same pattern as the existing `user_filter` implementation. Documentation and the example GitLab configuration file have been updated to describe the new setting.

The only prior attempt at this feature, https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/3218, was opened in 2017 and closed in 2021 with unresolved conflicts without ever landing. This MR is a fresh implementation from current master, not a revival of that branch.

## References

Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/334

## Screenshots or screen recordings

Verified live on a local GDK instance (LDAP + Premium/Ultimate license enabled) against real seed LDAP data (`ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com` contains one `posixGroup` entry, `example`, and two `groupofnames` entries, `group1`/`group2`). A group's **Settings → LDAP Synchronization** page calls `Adapter#groups` (via `GET /api/v4/ldap/:provider/groups.json`) to populate the "LDAP group cn" dropdown — exactly the method this MR modifies.

With `group_filter: '(cn=group*)'` set, `example` is correctly excluded from the dropdown (its `cn` doesn't match the pattern) while `group1`/`group2` remain — a realistic scenario: syncing only groups that follow a naming convention out of a directory that also holds unrelated entries:

| Before (no `group_filter`) | After (`group_filter: '(cn=group*)'`) |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](/uploads/d266fe12870633c247d5d537aed3900c/before.png) | ![after](/uploads/512270b9f23ed159f056d2a2f59c770e/after.png) |

`(cn=group*)` is just this demo's example filter — `group_filter`
accepts any valid RFC 4515 LDAP filter on any attribute, so entries
can be included or excluded by name, `objectClass`, or any other LDAP
attribute. `posixGroup` support itself is unaffected either way; a
filter targeting a specific `objectClass` (or leaving `group_filter`
unset) still works exactly as before.

Same result confirmed directly against the underlying API endpoint:

<details>
<summary>Real curl output, before/after</summary>

```
$ curl -s -H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v4/ldap/ldapmain/groups.json
# before (no group_filter):
[{"cn":"example"},{"cn":"group1"},{"cn":"group2"}]

# after (group_filter: '(cn=group*)'):
[{"cn":"group1"},{"cn":"group2"}]
```

</details>

## How to set up and validate locally

This is mostly a config-driven library change with no direct UI, so validation is via the RSpec suite covering the new behavior plus the full pre-existing suite for the two touched files (to confirm no regressions):

```
bin/rspec spec/lib/gitlab/auth/ldap/config_spec.rb ee/spec/lib/gitlab/auth/ldap/adapter_spec.rb
```

<details>
<summary>Real local run output (62 examples, 0 failures)</summary>

```
Finished in 18.91 seconds (files took 4 minutes 44 seconds to load)
62 examples, 0 failures
```

</details>

Each new spec was confirmed red against the pre-implementation code (via `git stash`) before the implementation was added, then confirmed green afterward, per the project's TDD convention.

To see it live: start from a GDK instance with license and enabled 'openladp' component, then add `group_filter: '<your filter>'` next to `group_base` in the LDAP server block of `config/gitlab.yml`, then restart `rails-web`, then visit a group's `Settings → LDAP Synchronization` page and check the `LDAP group cn` dropdown, or hit `GET /api/v4/ldap/:provider/groups.json` directly — as shown above.

## Disclosure

The CE config reader changes, the EE adapter modifications, the documentation and example-config updates, and all new spec coverage were done with AI assistance (Claude), verified via full red/green TDD (specs confirmed failing against pre-implementation code via `git stash`, then passing after) and by running the full pre-existing test suite for both touched files.

title: Support links in Mermaid diagrams via parent window delegation
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Fixes:

- #353389+, a four-year-old issue
- #583619+

## Solution

Links can't open from within the sandboxed iframe, so delegate their clicks to the parent window:

1. **Sandbox side** (`mermaid_sandbox.js`): intercept anchor clicks (left and middle)
   with `preventDefault` and post the `href` to the parent window
1. **Parent side** (`render_sandboxed_mermaid.js` and the rich text editor's `sandboxed_mermaid.vue`):
   handle the message in a message listener, validate the `href` with `isValidURL`,
   then open it in a new tab with a regular browsing context
1. Drop `allow-popups`, since the iframe no longer needs to open popups itself

Links now open in a new tab regardless of their `target` attribute.

```mermaid
---
config:
  fontSize: 14
---
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User
    participant Frame as Sandboxed iframe
    participant Parent as Parent window

    User->>Frame: clicks a link
    Frame->>Frame: intercept the click (preventDefault)
    Frame-)Parent: postMessage({ href })
    Parent->>Parent: verify the sender iframe (origin/source, existing)
    Parent->>Parent: validate the URL (isValidURL)
    create participant NewTab as New tab
    Parent->>NewTab: open
    Note over NewTab: regular browsing context
```

## Security considerations

- The sandbox restrictions are not relaxed (!214845+, which relaxed them, was rejected by AppSec).
  This MR goes the other way: it removes `allow-popups`, leaving the sandbox no way to open windows at all
- The URL is validated in the parent window with
  [`isValidURL`](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/secure_coding_guidelines/#gitlab-specific-libraries-for-mitigating-xss),
  on the receiving side of the message.
  The sender is verified by the existing origin/source checks. None of the validation is left to the sandboxed sender
- Even if XSS runs inside the sandbox, all it can do is have a validated http(s) URL opened in a new tab.
  Ordinary Markdown links can already send users to arbitrary URLs, so this adds no new attack surface
- Intercepting clicks inside the sandbox and having the parent validate and open them is the same pattern VS Code's webviews use

## References

- !251495+: introduced payload validation on the same message listener
- #354010+

## Verification

On Chrome, Firefox, and Safari.

## Notes

- I don't work on the frontend regularly — a careful look at this approach would be very helpful.

title: Add a previous-period trend column to GLQL analytics tables
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

A GLQL table on an analytics dashboard can now show a column with how each row moved against the period immediately before the dashboard's selected date range. A panel opts in with the same `showTrends: true` option under `visualization.options` that GLQL stat panels already use.

This was nearly free because the comparison-period plumbing already exists, added in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/253653 for the previous-period trend badge on GLQL stats. The dashboard GLQL data source already derives the shifted comparison query, `app/assets/javascripts/glql/components/common/resolver.vue` already runs it as a second query and exposes the result as `comparisonData`, and that data already reaches `DataPresenter` for every display type. The only gap was that `app/assets/javascripts/glql/components/presenters/data.vue` forwarded `comparisonData` to the stat presenter only. This MR forwards `comparisonData`, `trendMetric` and `source` to the table presenter too.

Rows are paired by a new pure helper, `app/assets/javascripts/glql/components/presenters/utils/table.js`, which builds a map of previous-period rows keyed by each dimension value's record `id`, deliberately not its display label — two distinct records can share a label (two users both named the same). `dimensionValue` is not used by the helper at all any more, so identity is fully decoupled from display. An object dimension value that carries no `id` cannot be told apart from another of its kind, so its row is left unpaired and reads as unknown rather than being matched on a label. The change is materialised onto a copy of each row, so the existing field sorter in `app/assets/javascripts/glql/core/sorter.js` orders the new column with no changes of its own — it reads values straight off the row and sorts `null` last.

The badge reuses `trendPresentationFor` from `app/assets/javascripts/glql/components/presenters/utils/stat.js`, the same function the stat badge uses, so colour, arrow direction, per-metric "which way is good" logic, and the accessibility tooltip are all shared. The cell renders the percentage on its own rather than the badge's `metaText`, because the column header already names the comparison (`metaText` reads as `23.4% vs prior`, which would be redundant under a `vs previous period` header). `trendChangeFor` and `formatChange` live in their own module, `app/assets/javascripts/glql/components/presenters/utils/trend.js`, shared by the stat utils and the table, so the sortable number and the rendered badge cannot disagree. `stat.js` imports them back. Still behaviour-neutral, existing stat specs pass unchanged.

A stat has exactly one metric, but a table can have several, so the panel names one with the `trendMetric` visualization option, matched against either the metric's alias or its base field name. A table with a single metric needs no config. A table with several metrics and no `trendMetric` reports a panel error. `trendMetric` sits in `visualization.options` next to the `showTrends` flag that turns the comparison query on in the first place, and is added to the `Options` definition in `ee/app/validators/json_schemas/analytics_visualization.json`. This is a temporary frontend-only trend, so it should not be exposed as part of the GLQL query language's own config surface — keeping it in the panel options puts the flag that enables the feature and the one setting that shapes it in the same place. The column header is fixed at `vs previous period`: the window it compares against follows the dashboard's date range filter, so per-panel wording would go stale as soon as the filter changed.

The column is dropped rather than shown wrong in three cases:

1. A date-bucket dimension (for example `created(weekly)`) — the bucket values are different dates in the shifted window, so pairing rows on dimension values would match nothing. Comparing a bucket against the same bucket one period back belongs in the aggregation engine, not here.
2. Two rows in either period sharing the same identity. Pairing either one would be a guess, so the column is dropped for that dimension. This is narrower than before, because identity now comes from a record `id` rather than a rendered label.
3. No comparison result, either because the panel did not ask for one or because the second query failed (the resolver swallows that failure to Sentry by design).

A row with no counterpart in the previous period renders an em dash, kept deliberately distinct from a neutral `0%` badge, which means the row was found and did not move. The comparison query is fetched once and never paginated, so a row past its extent is legitimately unknown too.

No dashboard panel enables this yet. The panel this was built for is the "Group comparison" table on the DAP Impact dashboard's Adoption tab, which still needs a group dimension in the aggregation engine and in the GLQL compiler before it can be a real group comparison. Those are tracked separately. This MR ships the capability and its tests only.

## References

- Issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/623357
- Builds on the stat trend badge: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/253653
- Group dimension on the `AiUsageEvents` engine: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254110
- Group dimension on the `DuoWorkflows` engine: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/617805
- GLQL compiler support for a `group` dimension: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/glql/-/issues/169
- Follow-up, the trend column appears one round-trip after the table because the two queries run sequentially: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/628335

## Screenshots or screen recordings

![Screen Recording 2026-09-09 at 1.43.10 PM.mov](/uploads/cbc4a6b2344a296d7261d36545a02251/Screen_Recording_2026-09-09_at_1.43.10_PM.mov){width=900 height=271}

## How to set up and validate locally

The trend column only appears on a **dashboard** panel. The comparison query is derived by the dashboard's GLQL data source from the date-range filter, so a standalone GLQL block in a comment or description has no filter to derive one from and can never show the column. It cannot be validated outside a dashboard.

1. Enable the option on the `Group comparison (WIP)` panel in `ee/lib/gitlab/analytics/dashboards/system/dap_impact.yaml`:

   ```diff
        visualization:
          type: Glql
          options:
            showActions: false
   +        showTrends: true
   +        trendMetric: usersCount
          data:
            type: glql
            query:
              glql: |
                display: table
                mode: analytics
                query: type = AgentPlatformSession and created >= "%{startDate}" and created <= "%{endDate}"
                dimensions: project as "Project"
                metrics: usersCount as "Users", totalCount as "Sessions"
                sort: usersCount desc
   ```
2. Seed AI usage data. ClickHouse must be enabled for analytics. The seeder takes one project per run and **skips any project with no members**, so add members first if needed:

   ```ruby
   # rails console — give a few projects members so the seeder has users to attribute events to
   users = User.human.active.limit(5)
   Project.where(id: [37, 45, 47]).each { |p| users.each { |u| p.add_developer(u) } }
   ```

   ```shell
   for pid in 37 45 47; do
     FILTER=ai_usage_stats PROJECT_ID=$pid SEED_AI_USAGE_STATS=1 bundle exec rake db:seed_fu
   done
   ```

   Each row in the table is one project, so seed several projects under the same group to get a table worth comparing.
3. `gdk restart rails-web` — the system dashboard YAML is read once per process and cached.
4. Visit `/explore/analytics_dashboards/dap_impact`, select the group containing the seeded projects in the filter at the top, and open the **Adoption** tab.
5. On the Group comparison panel, confirm:
   - A `vs previous period` column with arrow badges, coloured green for a rise in users and red for a fall.
   - Two aggregation GraphQL requests in the network tab rather than one.
   - Changing the date range recomputes the badges.
   - A project with no activity in the prior window shows an em dash, not `0%`.
   - Clicking the column header sorts by change, with em-dash rows last.
   - Removing `showTrends: true` renders the table exactly as before.

### Validating the guards

The first two replace the `glql:` body on the same panel; the third changes the panel options instead. All three are expected outcomes, not bugs.

**No trend column for a date-bucket dimension** — the buckets are different dates in the shifted window, so pairing rows on dimension values would match nothing:

```yaml
display: table
mode: analytics
query: type = AgentPlatformSession and created >= "%{startDate}" and created <= "%{endDate}"
dimensions: created(weekly)
metrics: usersCount as "Users"
sort: created asc
```

**No `trendMetric` needed when there is one metric** — remove the `trendMetric` option too, since a single metric is unambiguous and the column appears without it:

```yaml
display: table
mode: analytics
query: type = AgentPlatformSession and created >= "%{startDate}" and created <= "%{endDate}"
dimensions: project as "Project"
metrics: usersCount as "Users"
sort: usersCount desc
```

**A panel error for several metrics with no `trendMetric`** — keep both metrics from step 1 and remove the `trendMetric` line from the panel options. The panel surfaces `table display type requires `+ "`trendMetric`" + ` when several metrics are selected`.

Testing done: `yarn jest spec/frontend/glql ee/spec/frontend/glql spec/frontend/analytics/analytics_dashboards` passes, 2112 tests in 142 suites. ESLint and Prettier clean.

title: Fail dev fixtures when a new table has no seed data
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

A table with no rows is invisible to `db:migrate:multi-version-upgrade`. The upgrade-stop dump it runs against has nothing in the table, so any migration touching it is never really exercised. The `run-dev-fixtures-ee` job has been reporting these tables since !251786 without acting on them.

It now fails when a table the merge request itself adds holds no rows after seeding. Row-quality findings, such as a single row or a nullable column that never holds a null, stay as warnings.

Closes #451761.

## How to set up and validate locally

1. `bundle exec rspec spec/tasks/gitlab/seed/coverage_report_rake_spec.rb`
2. Point the task at a ref that adds a table and check the exit status: `RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rake "gitlab:seed:coverage_report[<ref>]"; echo $?`

<details>
<summary>Supporting evidence</summary>

### Why now

The report was left non-blocking on purpose. A read-only audit of the ten days after it shipped found it was scoped to the merge base rather than to the merge request's own diff, so it named every table master had gained since the branch point: 47 of 100 sampled merge requests that added no table at all were shown someone else's unseeded table, one of them 43 tables.

!253872 fixed that scoping. In the first 17 hours after it merged there were 1,401 merge request pipelines across 627 merge requests. Of the 128 jobs that produced a verdict, **none named a table**, while the old scoping would have named at least one on **44 of 100** merged-result pipelines. That 44% against the 47% measured before the fix confirms the populations are comparable, so the drop is the fix rather than a quiet week.

### The gate only fires on the merge request's own empty tables

Verified by running the real task and checking the process exit status, since an RSpec `SystemExit` assertion is not the same thing as CI seeing a non-zero exit:

| Scenario | Exit |
|----------|------|
| 11 real unseeded tables added | 1 |
| No tables added | 0 |
| Unreadable base ref, as on a shallow clone | 0 |
| No base ref, as on default-branch and scheduled pipelines | 0 |


These paths cannot fail a pipeline, each covered by a spec: no base ref, unreadable base ref, no tables added, entries that are not tables (views, deleted tables, background migrations), a `gitlab_schema` with no connection, and a dictionary entry whose table is absent from the schema. That last one is real rather than hypothetical: `merge_request_diff_commits_archived` has an entry in `db/docs/` but no `CREATE TABLE`, because it is the pre-partitioning table kept as a safety net during the swap.

### Expected load

One merge request added a table in the 17-hour window, and nine did over the preceding ten days, of which seven were unseeded. That is roughly five blocked merge requests a week, each a genuinely unseeded new table.

### Deliberately no bypass label

There is no opt-out label. The measured false-positive rate is zero, and a self-applied label makes the fix and the exception look identical. `pipeline::expedited` already skips the whole job for master-fixing and urgent reverts, so nothing is ever permanently blocked. If a legitimate case appears where a table cannot be seeded, adding a proportionate escape hatch is a few lines.

### Two limits worth stating

About 1.2% of jobs run a CI configuration predating the report, on a stale source branch or a stale stored merge ref, so the step does not exist for them at all. This is not introduced here and applies to every CI gate, but it means the check is not airtight.

The `run-dev-fixtures` FOSS variant does not copy `ee/db/fixtures/development/`, so it would judge EE tables unfairly. It never runs: `if-default-refs` cannot match the as-if-FOSS child pipeline, confirmed across seven of them.

title: Use throttled_error_message for the remaining rate limit responses
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

`Gitlab::ApplicationRateLimiter.throttled_error_message` exists so every rate limited response says the same thing, but a number of call sites still built the sentence themselves. Some wrapped it in `_()` and some did not, which is how wording drifts apart over time and how responses end up inconsistent depending on which endpoint a user happens to hit.

They now all call the helper. The string itself is unchanged and is still translated, because the helper wraps it in `_()`, so the message users see is identical and the msgid stays in `locale/gitlab.pot`.

Namespacing follows what each area already does: `Gitlab::` under `app/`, where the surrounding code uses that form, and `::Gitlab::` under `lib/` and `ee/`, where the code is nested and the existing call sites qualify it.

## References

- Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/619356
- The helper was introduced in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/245757

The issue lists fifteen files as of August. Two more carry the same literal today and are included here: `app/graphql/mutations/organizations/organization_users/create.rb` and `app/graphql/resolvers/concerns/search/search_rate_limitable.rb`.

## Differences

**Before:** seventeen call sites across sixteen files spelled out "This endpoint has been requested too many times. Try again later." themselves, some translated and some not, alongside others that already used the helper. Changing the wording meant finding every copy.

**After:** every rate limited response draws the message from one place. There is no user visible change: the same sentence is returned, still translated, from the same endpoints.

## How to set up and validate locally

```shell
grep -rn "This endpoint has been requested too many times" --include=*.rb app/ lib/ ee/ | grep -v _spec.rb
```

Only `lib/gitlab/application_rate_limiter.rb`, which defines the helper, should match. The msgid remains in `locale/gitlab.pot` because that definition still wraps the string in `_()`, so no regeneration is needed.

RuboCop passes on all sixteen files. Note that `Import::GithubService` is reformatted rather than only substituted: the shorter line made RuboCop ask for the modifier `if` form.

title: Cap Retry-After waits and drop URLs from attachment errors
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

`Gitlab::GithubImport::AttachmentsDownloader` is used by every GitHub import, so these two small hardening changes benefit all of them.

The downloader waited for exactly whatever `Retry-After` GitHub returned, falling back to 120 seconds only when the value was missing or zero. An unexpectedly large or malformed value could therefore park an import job for as long as the header claimed. The wait is now capped by `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RESET_IN`, one hour. The cap is applied after the default fallback, so a value already under an hour and the 120 second default behave exactly as before.

Download failures reported the raw download URL in their message. Those URLs can carry a short lived GitHub signed token, which then ends up in logs and error tracking. The message now names only the error code, on both the retriable and the non retriable path.

## References

- Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/628602
- Ported from the GitHub continuous sync proof of concept, but standalone: it does not depend on that epic
- LFS specific hardening is tracked separately in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/628601

## Differences

**Before:** a `Retry-After` of two hours meant a two hour wait, and there was no upper bound at all. A failed download raised "Error downloading file from https://..." with the full URL, token included.

**After:** any `Retry-After` above one hour waits one hour. A failed download raises "Error downloading attachment. Error code: 404" with no URL. Nothing else changes: values under an hour, the 120 second default, and the 403 without a header case all behave as they did.

One pre-existing edge worth naming so it is not mistaken for a regression: a negative `Retry-After` still passes through unchanged, as it did before. The cap uses `min`, which does not affect it. It is outside the two changes this issue scopes.

## How to set up and validate locally

```shell
bundle exec rspec spec/lib/gitlab/github_import/attachments_downloader_spec.rb
```

The new context is "when retry-after header exceeds RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RESET_IN", which sends a two hour value and expects `reset_in` of one hour. The existing 60 second and missing header cases are unchanged and still pass, which is the "no behaviour change under one hour" criterion. The three error message expectations now assert the URL free form.

title: Sync malware advisories for Premium via dependency_firewall availability
description:
## What

Widen the license gate for `PackageMetadata::MalwareAdvisoriesSyncWorker` so it syncs malware advisory data on Premium instances when the dependency firewall is available. Previously, the worker only ran for Ultimate (via `License.feature_available?(:dependency_scanning)`). The new gate is:

```ruby
License.feature_available?(:dependency_scanning) || Security::DependencyFirewall::Availability.instance_configurable?
```

This allows Premium instances with dependency firewall enabled to feed malicious advisories into the firewall's rule engine.

## Why the centralized availability check

An earlier version checked the `dependency_firewall` add-on purchase directly (`GitlabSubscriptions::AddOnPurchase.for_active_add_ons(:dependency_firewall, :instance)`), but this add-on is not registered in the system, making the check a permanent no-op.

`Security::DependencyFirewall::Availability.instance_configurable?` is the single source of truth for instance-level dependency firewall availability. It already works for Premium, combining the `dependency_firewall_phase1` feature flag and the `dependency_firewall` license in one place.

## Behaviour

| Tier / entitlement | Sync runs? |
|---|---|
| Free / Starter | No |
| Premium, dependency firewall not available | No |
| Premium, dependency firewall available (`dependency_firewall_phase1` enabled and `dependency_firewall` licensed) | Yes |
| Ultimate | Yes (via `dependency_scanning`) |

Notes:

- No change on GitLab.com: the instance is Ultimate, so it syncs via `dependency_scanning`. `instance_configurable?` returns `false` on SaaS, so GitLab.com does not rely on the Premium path.
- The whole sync stays behind the `sync_malware_advisories` feature flag, and the Premium path is additionally gated by `dependency_firewall_phase1` (disabled by default). This introduces no default behaviour change, so there is no changelog entry.

## Keep CVS malware findings Ultimate-only

Reviewer @hbakergitlab pointed out that the malware advisory rows this worker syncs also feed a second, separate pipeline: `PackageMetadata::MalwareAdvisoryIngestionService` publishes `IngestedMalwareAdvisoryEvent` (gated only by the default-on `ingest_malware_advisories` flag), which `PackageMetadata::GlobalMalwareAdvisoryScanWorker` consumes (gated only by the default-on `cvs_malware_advisories` flag) and turns into `Vulnerability` records via `Gitlab::VulnerabilityScanning::MalwareAdvisoryScanner`. That path had no license or tier check.

Continuous vulnerability scanning (CVS) malicious-package findings are Ultimate-only. Because this MR lets the sync populate advisories on Premium, that path would otherwise create Ultimate-tier vulnerability records on Premium.

Fix: `MalwareAdvisoryScanner#cvs_enabled_for_project?` now returns early unless `project.licensed_feature_available?(:dependency_scanning)`, mirroring `cvs_for_dependency_scanning_available`. CVS malware findings are only created for Ultimate-eligible projects, regardless of where the sync ran.

Note this also normalizes existing behaviour on GitLab.com: non-Ultimate namespaces will no longer get CVS malware findings from this path (they should not have, per the Ultimate-only docs). The equivalent gap on the public CVE CVS path (`Gitlab::VulnerabilityScanning::AdvisoryScanner`) is handled in a separate merge request.

## Related

- Part of and closes: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/606640
- Based on this note: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/606640#note_3797883183
- The SSCS add-on gate was already removed in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/246641 (related to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/602432)

## Tests

Updated the worker spec in `ee/spec/workers/package_metadata/malware_advisories_sync_worker_spec.rb`:

- Added a context for when neither `dependency_scanning` nor the dependency firewall is available (the worker does not run).
- Added a context for when the dependency firewall is available on Premium (the worker runs).
- Both contexts stub `Security::DependencyFirewall::Availability.instance_configurable?` at the boundary.

Updated the scanner spec in `ee/spec/lib/gitlab/vulnerability_scanning/malware_advisory_scanner_spec.rb`:

- Stubbed `dependency_scanning` availability and added a context asserting no vulnerability is created for a project that is not licensed for dependency scanning.

title: Add merge request risk classification widget
description:
## What does this MR do and why? Surfaces a merge request's risk assessment on the page as its own widget: a tier and confidence pill in the title, and an expandable panel with the rationale and the signals that drove the score. The widget's status icon reflects where the assessment is in its lifecycle (`pending`, `queued`, `complete`, or `failed`), not the result itself - a completed assessment always shows the same success icon no matter how risky the score turned out, since the tier and confidence pills already say that. Whether the result is shown follows the score, not the status. A refresh leaves the previous score in place, so a queued row can still hold a full result. In that case the widget keeps showing that result and reports that it is updating, rather than hiding a score the reviewer could already see. A failed run is treated as a hard stop instead, because there is no result left to trust. Visibility follows the `riskAssessment` GraphQL field: the widget renders only when that field returns a record. What gates the field is decided in the backend half of this change, https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254419. > [!NOTE] > This is an initial design for customer 0 experimentation. The final design is not defined yet and is being discussed by the product designers. > The whole feature is under development and is not being used yet. ## References Part of https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/epics/23131 (Phase 1) Part of https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/609295 Backend half of this change (GraphQL gate and the N+1 fix): https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254419 ## Screenshots or screen recordings **Widget collapsed, showing the tier and confidence pills** ![Screenshot_2026-09-08_at_20.59.42](/uploads/78bf46bec9153f170bc4102e44650701/Screenshot_2026-09-08_at_20.59.42.png) Widget expanded, showing the rationale, and the signals that contributed to the score: ![Screenshot_2026-09-08_at_21.11.15](/uploads/71436157c868666fe3efe0a4b74bd3bf/Screenshot_2026-09-08_at_21.11.15.png) Widget as it will look like when Duo session is available: ![Kapture_2026-09-03_at_13.43.07](/uploads/455532b119729cbef26366ac3f087c65/Kapture_2026-09-03_at_13.43.07.mp4){width=832 height=600} ## How to set up and validate locally The widget renders only when the `riskAssessment` GraphQL field returns a record. On `master` that field is gated by a feature flag and the `ai_features` license: 1. Enable the feature flag globally: `Feature.enable(:duo_mr_risk_classification)` 1. Use an Ultimate license, so `ai_features` is available to the project. 1. Open the merge request's Overview tab. The widget shows up between the Sessions widget and the approvals widget. Once https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254419 merges, the gate changes: the `risk_classification/v1` foundational flow also has to be enabled for the project. Edit Duo settings for the root namespace at http://gdk.test:3000/groups/gitlab-duo/-/edit#js-gitlab-duo-settings and switch the flow on: ![Screenshot_2026-09-03_at_13.34.04](/uploads/a91804eeeb121853f4a114e60df0c54f/Screenshot_2026-09-03_at_13.34.04.png){width=900 height=307} ### Checking each state Manual setup is needed because no worker writes risk assessment records yet. The widget only reads a database record; it does not compute a score itself. As a result, a reviewer cannot reach the widget's different states through normal product use, and must create the records by hand. Save the script below to a file and run it with `bundle exec rails runner`, passing the number of the scenario you want to test. The script sets the database record for that scenario and prints the values the GraphQL API will expose, so you can confirm the data before you judge the rendering. After each run, hard reload the merge request page. A normal reload can serve an old cached bundle, because the widget's JavaScript loads as a separate lazy chunk. Running the script deletes any existing risk assessment and Duo session for the merge request before it writes the new scenario data, and prints each deleted record. If you have a real Duo session on that merge request, running a scenario deletes it. ```shell # defaults to gitlab-duo/test!1 bundle exec rails runner risk_scenario.rb 11 # or point it at your own merge request PROJECT=my-group/my-project MR_IID=7 bundle exec rails runner risk_scenario.rb 11 ``` Two states come from the network layer, not the database, so the script cannot produce them. To see the loading state, open DevTools, throttle the network to slow 3G, and reload the page. To see the fetch error state, open the DevTools network request blocking panel, block the `/api/graphql` request, and reload the page. ### Scenarios Scores map onto tiers by fixed bounds: low `0-24`, medium `25-49`, high `50-74`, critical `75-100`. Confidence uses the same bounds with its own labels. **Visibility** | # | Record state | Expected | | - | ------------ | -------- | | `1` | No assessment row | Widget does not render at all | **Before a score exists.** No pills, and the panel cannot be expanded. | # | Record state | Expected | | - | ------------ | -------- | | `2` | `pending` | "Risk assessment pending", neutral icon | | `3` | `queued`, no earlier score | "New risk assessment queued", notice icon | | `4` | `failed`, no score | "Risk assessment failed", failed icon | | `19` | `failed`, earlier score kept | Same as `4`. The old score must not appear in pills | **Re-assessment.** A refresh leaves the previous score in place, so a queued row can still hold a full result. | # | Record state | Expected | | - | ------------ | -------- | | `20` | `queued` over an earlier result | "Risk assessment updating", earlier pills and panel stay visible | **Tier and confidence bands.** All `complete`, all show the success icon. | # | Score / confidence | Expected pills | | - | ------------------ | -------------- | | `5` | 10 / 60 | `Low risk` success, `High confidence` success | | `6` | 30 / 40 | `Medium risk` warning, `Medium confidence` warning | | `7` | 60 / 10 | `High risk` danger, `Low confidence` danger | | `8` | 90 / 90 | `Critical risk` danger, `Very high confidence` success | **Panel contents.** Expand the widget to see these. | # | Record state | Expected | | - | ------------ | -------- | | `9` | No rationale, no signals | Panel opens but is empty | | `10` | Rationale only | Rationale, and no signal list | | `11` | Rationale and three signals | Rationale, then the signal list | | `12` | Low confidence, two missing signals | "Based on a partial picture" notice above the list | | `13` | `diff_sha` differs from the head SHA | Staleness notice at the top of the panel | | `14` | Signal key with no registered label | Row falls back to the raw key | | `15` | Signal with no detail | Label only, and no grey sub-line | | `17` | `complete` but no score | No pills, and the panel cannot be expanded | | `18` | Missing signals, some keys unregistered | Notice names only the signals it can resolve. Unregistered keys are left out | | `21` | Missing signals, no key registered | Notice is not rendered, because it would name nothing | **Duo session.** These cover the "View session" button and the panel it opens. | # | Record state | Expected | | - | ------------ | -------- | | `16` | Session recorded on the assessment | Small "View session" button in the header row | | `22` | Session recorded, plus a staged transcript | The button opens the Duo panel, and the panel shows a six message transcript | Scenario `22` writes two extra rows: a `risk_classification/v1` workflow, and one checkpoint that holds the transcript. It sets the workflow to `finished`, so the panel renders the transcript instead of polling for updates. The transcript in scenario `22` is invented. No assessment run has produced a session yet, because the scoring worker does not exist. The message wording is plausible for the flow, and the numbers agree with the assessment row, but treat it as staged data. Do not read it as a specification of what the flow will emit.
risk_scenario.rb ```ruby # Manual test harness for the merge request risk assessment widget. # # bundle exec rails runner risk_scenario.rb <1-22> # PROJECT=my-group/my-project MR_IID=7 bundle exec rails runner risk_scenario.rb 11 # # Every scenario deletes the records it owns before writing new ones, so a run # never depends on what an earlier run left behind. The merge request, the # project and the users are never touched. SCENARIO = ARGV[0].to_s WORKFLOW_DEFINITION = 'risk_classification/v1' project = Project.find_by_full_path(ENV.fetch('PROJECT', 'gitlab-duo/test')) abort 'Project not found. Set PROJECT=.' unless project mr = project.merge_requests.find_by(iid: ENV.fetch('MR_IID', '1')) abort 'Merge request not found. Set MR_IID=.' unless mr head = mr.diff_head_sha # Every risk classification session recorded against this merge request, # whichever goal form wrote it. A Duo session for anything else is left alone. def related_workflows(project, mr) ::Ai::DuoWorkflows::Workflow .where(project_id: project.id, workflow_definition: WORKFLOW_DEFINITION) .where('merge_request_id = ? OR goal = ?', mr.id, mr.iid.to_s) end # Deletions are printed rather than silent, because a session recorded by a real # flow run looks the same to this scope as one an earlier scenario left behind. def reset!(project, mr) assessment = mr.reload.risk_assessment if assessment puts "reset: assessment ##{assessment.id} (status #{assessment.status})" assessment.risk_outcomes.delete_all(:delete_all) assessment.destroy! end related_workflows(project, mr).each do |workflow| puts "reset: session ##{workflow.id} (status #{workflow.status}, " \ "#{workflow.checkpoints.count} checkpoints)" # delete_all with no argument nullifies the foreign key, and every one of # these columns is NOT NULL, so the strategy has to be passed explicitly. %i[checkpoint_writes checkpoint_blobs checkpoint_headers checkpoints events merge_request_links work_item_links note_links pipeline_links workflows_workloads].each do |association| workflow.public_send(association).delete_all(:delete_all) end workflow.destroy! end end # duo_workflow_id is a foreign key, so the session has to be a real row. def create_session(project, mr, transcript: false) user = User.find_by(username: ENV.fetch('SESSION_USER', 'root')) abort 'Session user not found. Set SESSION_USER=.' unless user workflow = ::Ai::DuoWorkflows::Workflow.create!( project_id: project.id, user_id: user.id, merge_request_id: mr.id, workflow_definition: WORKFLOW_DEFINITION, goal: mr.iid.to_s, agent_privileges: [3, 4, 5], pre_approved_agent_privileges: [], environment: :web ) # Finished, so the panel renders what it has instead of polling for updates. workflow.update_columns(status: 3) add_transcript(project, workflow, mr) if transcript workflow.id end # The transcript is invented. No assessment run has produced a session yet, # because the scoring worker does not exist, so treat it as staged data. def add_transcript(project, workflow, mr) now = Time.current entry = lambda do |type, content, offset, tool: nil| { 'message_type' => type, 'role' => type == 'user' ? 'user' : 'assistant', 'status' => 'success', 'content' => content, 'timestamp' => (now - offset).iso8601(6), 'tool_info' => tool, 'correlation_id' => nil, 'message_sub_type' => nil, 'message_id' => "#{type}-#{SecureRandom.uuid}", 'additional_context' => [] } end log = [ entry.call('user', "Assess the risk of merge request !#{mr.iid}.", 120), entry.call('agent', 'Reading the merge request and the files it changes.', 110), entry.call('tool', 'Fetched the merge request.', 100, tool: { 'name' => 'get_merge_request' }), entry.call('tool', 'Read app/services/tokens/refresh_service.rb.', 90, tool: { 'name' => 'read_file' }), entry.call('tool', 'Searched for specs that cover the changed path.', 80, tool: { 'name' => 'grep' }), entry.call('agent', 'The change adds a token refresh path. It widens the authorization surface and ' \ 'ships without a matching spec. I scored the risk 60 and the confidence 80.', 70) ] ::Ai::DuoWorkflows::Checkpoint.create!( workflow: workflow, project_id: project.id, thread_ts: Gitlab::Utils.uuid_v7, checkpoint: { 'channel_values' => { 'ui_chat_log' => log } }, metadata: { 'source' => 'risk_scenario.rb' } ) end SIGNALS_FULL = [ { 'signal' => 'test_evidence.untested', 'contribution' => 12.0, 'detail' => 'app/services/tokens/refresh_service.rb has no matching spec' }, { 'signal' => 'diff_shape.churn', 'contribution' => 6.0, 'detail' => '412 lines changed across 9 files' }, { 'signal' => 'ownership.author_not_owner', 'contribution' => 3.0, 'detail' => nil } ].freeze RATIONALE = 'Adds a token refresh path that widens the authorization surface, ' \ 'and the new branch ships without a matching spec.' # status, score, confidence, rationale, signal_breakdown, missing_signals, session, diff_sha # # session is :none, :session for a bare session, or :transcript for one the Duo # panel can render. The row is created only for the scenario being applied. SCENARIOS = { '2' => [0, nil, nil, nil, [], [], :none, head], '3' => [1, nil, nil, nil, [], [], :none, head], '4' => [3, nil, nil, nil, [], [], :none, head], '19' => [3, 60, 80, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, [], :none, head], '20' => [1, 60, 60, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, [], :session, head], '5' => [2, 10, 60, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, [], :none, head], '6' => [2, 30, 40, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, [], :none, head], '7' => [2, 60, 10, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, %w[test_coverage ai_authorship], :none, head], '8' => [2, 90, 90, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, [], :none, head], '9' => [2, 60, 80, nil, [], [], :none, head], '10' => [2, 60, 80, RATIONALE, [], [], :none, head], '11' => [2, 60, 80, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, [], :none, head], '12' => [2, 60, 10, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, %w[test_coverage ai_authorship], :none, head], '13' => [2, 60, 80, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, [], :none, 'dead' + ('beef' * 9)], '14' => [2, 60, 80, nil, [{ 'signal' => 'authorization', 'contribution' => 21.0, 'detail' => 'app/policies/token_policy.rb:4' }], [], :none, head], '15' => [2, 60, 80, nil, [{ 'signal' => 'revert.reverts_prior_change', 'contribution' => 5.0, 'detail' => nil }], [], :none, head], '16' => [2, 60, 80, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, [], :session, head], '17' => [2, nil, nil, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, [], :none, head], '18' => [2, 60, 10, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, %w[test_coverage ai_authorship authentication database_migration], :none, head], '21' => [2, 60, 10, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, %w[authentication database_migration], :none, head], '22' => [2, 60, 80, RATIONALE, SIGNALS_FULL, [], :transcript, head] }.freeze if SCENARIO == '1' reset!(project, mr) puts 'Scenario 1: no assessment row -- the widget must not render at all.' puts "flag enabled? #{Feature.enabled?(:duo_mr_risk_classification, project.root_ancestor)}" exit end attrs = SCENARIOS[SCENARIO] abort "Unknown scenario #{SCENARIO.inspect}. Valid: 1-22" unless attrs status, score, confidence, rationale, breakdown, missing, session, diff_sha = attrs reset!(project, mr) session_id = case session when :session then create_session(project, mr) when :transcript then create_session(project, mr, transcript: true) end a = MergeRequests::RiskAssessment.new(merge_request: mr, project_id: project.id) a.diff_sha = diff_sha a.score = score a.confidence = confidence a.rationale = rationale a.signal_breakdown = breakdown a.missing_signals = missing a.duo_workflow_id = session_id a.assessed_at = status == 2 ? Time.current : nil a.scoring_function_version = 'v1' a.classification = {} a.domain_tags = [] a.write_attribute(:status, status) a.save! a.reload # Mirror what the GraphQL type actually exposes to the widget. puts "== Scenario #{SCENARIO} applied on #{project.full_path}!#{mr.iid} ==" puts "status #{a.status_name} (#{a.status})" puts "riskTier #{a.risk_tier.inspect} (score #{a.score.inspect})" puts "confidenceTier #{a.confidence_tier.inspect} (confidence #{a.confidence.inspect})" puts "stale #{a.diff_sha != head} (diff_sha #{a.diff_sha[0, 12]} vs head #{head[0, 12]})" puts "rationale #{a.rationale ? a.rationale[0, 60] + '...' : nil.inspect}" puts "duoWorkflowId #{a.duo_workflow_id.inspect}" puts 'contributingSignals' a.signal_breakdown.each do |s| label = Gitlab::Duo::RiskClassification::SignalsExtractor.label_for(s['signal']) puts " #{s['signal']} -> label=#{label.inspect} detail=#{s['detail'].inspect}" end puts 'missingSignals' if a.missing_signals.empty? puts ' (none)' else labels = a.missing_signals.map { |k| Gitlab::Duo::RiskClassification::SignalsExtractor.label_for(k) } a.missing_signals.zip(labels).each { |k, l| puts " #{k} -> label=#{l.inspect}" } puts " joined as the widget renders it: #{labels.compact.join(', ').inspect}" end ```

title: Retry transient HttpIO chunk failures behind a feature flag
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

`Gitlab::HttpIO` reads remote files (archived CI job traces, job artifacts) from object storage as a series of 128 KB HTTP range requests over one keep-alive session.

Object storage fails a small fraction of requests: refused or dropped TLS connections, transient 5xx. Because one read issues many chunk requests, a small per-request failure rate compounds into a much higher per-read failure rate, and today any single failed chunk fails the whole read and surfaces to the user as a 500.

On GitLab Dedicated this shows up as SSL handshake failures (`SSL_connect returned=6 errno=107 state=SSLv3/TLS write client hello`) on reads of `GET /api/:version/projects/:id/jobs/:job_id/trace`.

`Net::HTTP` already retries once, but does not cover these cases:

- The TLS handshake in `Net::HTTP.start` happens outside `Net::HTTP#transport_request`.
- Response status codes are not errors to it at all.

This MR adds retry handling behind the feature flag `http_io_retry_transient_errors`, disabled by default. With the flag off, the original code path runs unchanged: the two paths are separate methods, so disabling the flag is a real kill switch rather than a no-op branch through new code.

What it retries:

- Transport errors: TLS errors, connection resets, DNS failures, EOF mid-body, malformed responses.
- Response codes 429, 500, 502, 503, 504.

What the added retry loop does not retry:

- Other 4xx. An expired presigned object storage URL returns 403, and retrying only adds latency before the same failure.
- Open/read/write timeout errors. Repeating these waits would add latency to user-facing requests. Existing `Net::HTTP` retry behavior, including its read-timeout retry, is unchanged.

Budget: up to 3 additional HttpIO attempts shared across every chunk an instance fetches, on top of existing `Net::HTTP` retries. The budget persists across calls to `read` and `readline`; it does not reset per chunk or per read call.

Backoff: 100ms base, doubled per retry and jittered, for 0.35–1.05 seconds of total sleep when all 3 retries are used. Network time is additional: retriable errors can occur after slow I/O, and a subsequent attempt can time out. This bounds retry attempts and sleep, not total read duration.

This MR also adds a new Prometheus counter, `gitlab_http_io_chunk_retries_total`, labelled by reason (the error class, or `http_<code>`), because no existing metric distinguishes a clean request from one that needed a retry. This is what makes the rollout readable.

## How to set up and validate locally

Run:

```
bundle exec rspec spec/lib/gitlab/http_io_spec.rb
```

Validated on commit `842a69311c03d3d082ac2d29e4ddc63e2d7e9097`:

- RSpec: **63 examples, 0 failures**, including enabled and disabled flag paths.
- `bundle exec rubocop lib/gitlab/http_io.rb spec/lib/gitlab/http_io_spec.rb`: **2 files inspected, no offenses**.
- [Latest merged-results pipeline](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/pipelines/2822136793): **passed**.

The specs cover the retry paths, including one run against a real keep-alive HTTP server on localhost, because WebMock intercepts above the socket layer and cannot exercise real transport failures.

## References

- Reported problem: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/604514
- Parent epic for HttpIO work: https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/23204
- Feature flag rollout issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/623429

## Screenshots or screen recordings

Not applicable: no visible UI changes.

## MR acceptance checklist

- Prior Duo findings are addressed: preserve the original EOFError as the cause, keep existing single-attempt failure specs on the disabled path, and isolate retry metrics and backoff in specs.
- The feature flag is disabled by default, with rollout and rollback tracked in the linked rollout issue.
- No changelog entry is needed while the behavior is behind a default-off flag.
- No user documentation changes are needed for this internal retry behavior.

title: Move duoChatGlobalState out of the sidebar state module
description:
## Why

`duoChatGlobalState` is a shared reactive object created with the `observable` helper from `~/lib/utils/observable`. It holds Duo Chat panel state: chat mode, focus flag, last route per tab, and drag width.

It currently lives in `app/assets/javascripts/super_sidebar/state.js`, which is listed on `INFECTION_BLOCKLIST` in `config/helpers/context_aliases_shared.js`. During the Vue 3 migration, most modules that reach Vue are built twice, once per Vue runtime. A blocklisted module is the exception: the build keeps one single copy.

The `observable` helper keeps one canonical value in a `globalThis` registry and builds one reactive mirror per Vue runtime that loads the module. If the module is never duplicated, only one mirror is ever built, tied to whichever Vue version loaded it first.

Today every consumer of `duoChatGlobalState` runs on Vue 2, so this is safe. It stops being safe when the Duo panel renders on Vue 3 (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/623999). The Vue 3 panel would read the Vue 2 mirror. Vue 2 tracks dependencies with `Object.defineProperty` getters, and a Vue 3 render effect reading that object does not register with them. The panel would render once and never update.

## What

Move `duoChatGlobalState` to a new file `ee/app/assets/javascripts/ai/state.js` and repoint every import. Move `CHAT_MODES`, the enum for its `chatMode` field, into the same file. No change to the values, the observable key `'duo_chat_global_state'`, or any consumer logic.

## How

The new module is not on the blocklist, so the build duplicates it like any other module. Each Vue runtime builds its own mirror, and `observable` syncs them through the shared registry, which is what it is designed to do.

`CHAT_MODES` lived in `app/assets/javascripts/super_sidebar/constants.js`, but no sidebar code read it. Every consumer is under `ee/app/assets/javascripts/ai/`, and `ee/ai/tanuki_bot/constants.js` re-exported it, so one value had two import paths. It now lives beside the state it describes, the re-export is gone, and every importer uses `ee/ai/state`.

**Reviewer note:** the infection scanner reports both modules as `infected: true`. The difference is only that `super_sidebar/state.js` has a blocklist entry that overrides this at build time. That asymmetry is what the fix relies on.

## How to verify

This is a pure refactor, our test suite would cover these.

**Note:** `duo_agentic_chat_state_manager_spec.js` needs `ee/frontend_islands/apps/duo_next/dist` built locally, or Jest cannot resolve a virtual mock and the suite fails to run. This is unrelated to the change.

### Not covered by this MR

Jest pins one `VUE_VERSION` per process (`jest.config.base.js`), so the "syncs across multiple mirrors" case in `spec/frontend/lib/utils/observable_spec.js` cannot exercise the cross-version path. Only a feature spec that renders a Vue 3 page next to the Vue 2 panel, or the reverse, can confirm cross-runtime updates. That check must happen before the Duo panel Vue 3 feature flag is enabled. It does not block this MR.

**Note:** Tests will have to be covered before we merge https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/252443 

## References

- Part of https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/623999 (tracking issue for moving global bundles, including the Duo panel, to Vue 3)
- Builds on https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/252293 (merged; gives the Duo panel its own bundle, which is what makes it renderable on Vue 3)
- Related, not a dependency: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/252286 (open; extends `vue3_migration.yml` to global bundles, needed by the follow-up MR that declares the Duo panel rollout)
- Parent epic https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/epics/6252
- Prompted the `CHAT_MODES` move: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/252442#note_3820664807

title: Add instance setting to auto-index root namespaces for Orbit
description:
## What does this MR do and why? Adds an instance setting to automatically enroll top-level groups into Orbit indexing on GitLab Self-Managed, similar to Zoekt. This gives administrators an "index everything" option without using the Rails console or enrolling groups one at a time. Turning the setting off keeps existing enrollments. ## References Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/606375 ## Screenshots or screen recordings | Before | After | | ------ | ----- | | ![image](/uploads/73d4d9ccc064e6e04a3a396e3a6995e3/image.png){width=864 height=600} | ![image](/uploads/bc6f77d8351e992daed8e4cac301f8e9/image.png){width=864 height=600} | After enabling the setting: ![image](/uploads/37309df0693d79fec0b1ffc99dc8f84c/image.png){width=864 height=600} ## Database The worker batches top-level groups in ID ranges of 1,000 rows before applying the anti-join within each bounded range. The outer batch query uses the partial index `index_groups_on_parent_id_id`, and the anti-join uses the unique index `index_knowledge_graph_enabled_namespaces_on_root_namespace_id`. The query below shows one batch with a reduced batch size of two to demonstrate both ID boundaries generated by `EachBatch`: ```sql SELECT "namespaces"."id" FROM "namespaces" LEFT OUTER JOIN "knowledge_graph_enabled_namespaces" "knowledge_graph_enabled_namespace" ON "knowledge_graph_enabled_namespace"."root_namespace_id" = "namespaces"."id" WHERE "namespaces"."type" = 'Group' AND "namespaces"."parent_id" IS NULL AND "namespaces"."id" >= 22 AND "namespaces"."id" < 27 AND "namespaces"."parent_id" IS NULL AND "knowledge_graph_enabled_namespace"."root_namespace_id" IS NULL; ``` ```text Nested Loop Anti Join (cost=0.29..4.74 rows=1 width=8) (actual time=0.198..0.200 rows=2 loops=1) Buffers: shared hit=6 read=1 -> Index Only Scan using index_groups_on_parent_id_id on namespaces (cost=0.13..2.36 rows=1 width=8) (actual time=0.194..0.195 rows=2 loops=1) Index Cond: ((parent_id IS NULL) AND (parent_id IS NULL) AND (id >= 22) AND (id < 27)) Heap Fetches: 2 Buffers: shared hit=2 read=1 -> Index Only Scan using index_knowledge_graph_enabled_namespaces_on_root_namespace_id on knowledge_graph_enabled_namespaces knowledge_graph_enabled_namespace (cost=0.15..2.37 rows=1 width=8) (actual time=0.001..0.001 rows=0 loops=2) Index Cond: (root_namespace_id = namespaces.id) Heap Fetches: 0 Buffers: shared hit=4 Planning: Buffers: shared hit=57 Planning Time: 0.343 ms Execution Time: 0.210 ms ``` ## How to set up and validate locally 1. Configure Orbit and enable the `knowledge_graph` feature flag. 1. Sign in as an administrator and visit `/admin/orbit`. 1. Select **Index root namespaces automatically**, then **Save changes**. 1. Run `Analytics::KnowledgeGraph::AutoIndexWorker.new.perform` in the Rails console. 1. Verify that top-level groups are enrolled and existing enrollments remain after clearing the setting. 1. Run `bundle exec rake gitlab:orbit:info` and check the setting value.
Agent context - implementation decisions and verification ### Implementation notes - Current master already has the Admin > Orbit page and `gitlab:orbit:info` backed by `Analytics::KnowledgeGraph::InfoService`. Unlike https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/246563, this MR extends those components and keeps the registry under `Analytics::KnowledgeGraph` instead of adding parallel `Orbit` classes and a bounded context. - Orbit accepts top-level group namespaces, so the scope excludes personal namespaces. - Disabling the setting never deletes enrollments. - The JSONB column and object constraint use separate migrations so the constraint uses the standard non-transactional helper. - The request spec replaces the reference MR's controller spec. - Review feedback from the reference MR is included: the help path omits `.md`, docs use current shortcodes and one sentence per line, the setting definition and OpenAPI entries are present, worker deltas are exact, and `locale/gitlab.pot` is regenerated. ### Verification - Focused RSpec suite: 1,512 examples, 0 failures, 5 existing pending examples. - RuboCop on all changed Ruby files. - HAML lint, Markdown lint, Vale, OpenAPI validation, gettext extraction, queue generation, and pre-push checks. - Migration rollback and reapply in GDK. The info task reports: ```text Deployment: Self-managed License :orbit available: yes Index root namespaces automatically: yes ```

It helps you analyze changes to reduce risks in quality, performance, reliability, security, and maintainability. - [x] The setting defaults to off and is gated to self-managed, licensed instances. - [x] The worker is idempotent, add-only, batched, and safe against concurrent inserts. - [x] The setting is documented in product docs and the application settings OpenAPI schema. - [x] Generated schema, queue, and translation files are updated. - [x] Run `db:gitlabcom-database-testing` before database review.

title: Document the offline v3 license download procedure
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

An air-gapped instance gets v3 license data by mirroring the whole license bucket with `gsutil`, which copies both format prefixes and every delta, about 2.4 GB today. This adds a second procedure next to the malware advisory one it mirrors: it asks the distribution service which archives make up the current snapshot and downloads only those, for only the registries the instance has enabled. The script is the malware one with the licenses endpoints swapped in, reading `url` instead of `signed_url` because the licenses bucket is public, so the two stay easy to diff.

The `rsync` step is scoped to `v3/` on both sides rather than the whole `licenses/` directory, since `--delete` against the parent would remove an existing `v2/` tree that the instance still reads until the cutover. Troubleshooting covers the registry-id naming, the missing checkpoint case, and one licenses-specific check, no license carrying an `spdx_expression` after a sync means the instance read the v2 layout.

## What does this MR do and why?

Renames the AI Catalog built-in tool `get_previous_session_context` to `get_session_context` to match the rename already shipped in the AI Gateway (gitlab-org/modelops/applied-ml/code-suggestions/ai-assist!6283). The numeric tool id (58) is unchanged, to preserve tool selections persisted in `Ai::Catalog::ItemVersion#def_tools`.

Updates the tool's metadata in `ee/lib/ai/catalog/built_in_tool_definitions.rb` and its key in the privilege group mapping in `ee/lib/ai/tool_rules/registry.rb` — this one matters functionally, since the old key would have dropped the tool out of `all_tool_names`, `default_permission_of`, `category_for`, and `action_type_of`. Also updates a stale comment in `ee/app/graphql/ee/types/query_type.rb` and the test strings in `ee/spec/requests/api/graphql/ai/catalog/built_in_tools_spec.rb`.

Also adds a post-deploy data migration for existing `ai_tool_rules` rows left on the old tool name. Without it, an admin's Deny or Ask on this tool becomes invisible in the governance UI and silently falls back to auto-allow, since `read_only_gitlab` is in `DEFAULT_PREAPPROVED_GROUPS`. title: Trigger risk classification from the flow trigger platform
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Nothing started a risk classification. The flow existed, a project could turn it on, and it still never ran: something had to call it, and that something was a service and a worker written only for this one flow.

The flow now declares its own triggers instead. It runs when a merge request opens and when one changes from draft to ready, so turning the flow on for a project is the only switch a user touches. That is how every other foundational flow works.

Getting there needed one thing the platform did not have. A flow sometimes has to put a record in place before it starts, and there was no way to say so from a flow definition. Two optional callbacks, `before_start` and `after_start`, close that: each takes the triggered resource, each defaults to nothing. Risk classification uses `before_start` to record that a classification is running, which is what lets the widget tell "running" from "never ran" once it ships.

`before_start` fires after the last check that can still refuse a run, not before it. Otherwise a refused run would leave a record claiming a classification is in progress.

**This is deliberately incomplete.** Nothing scores the claims a run sends back, and nothing expires a record whose run goes quiet. Both arrive with the scoring work, which is also when `duo_mr_risk_classification` can be turned on. Until then a triggered run stores its claims and stops there. Left as a draft for that reason.

What the flow is told about the merge request it classifies is a separate change, https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254877. Both target master and neither depends on the other, but a run started from this branch alone stops at the agent's input validation, because the agent platform config expects the inputs that MR sends. Check out both to watch a run reach the agent.

## References

- Issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/609293
- What the flow is told about the merge request: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254877, paired with https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/modelops/applied-ml/code-suggestions/ai-assist/-/merge_requests/6872
- Scoring and orchestration, which fill in the rest: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/253486 and https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/253762
- Phase 1 epic: https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/epics/23131

## Screenshots or screen recordings

Not applicable. No user-facing surface changes here: the widget that reads the record ships in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/251381.

## How to set up and validate locally

The flow is `ultimate_only`, so the GDK needs an Ultimate licence. Two feature flags matter:

```ruby
# Gates the flow itself. Without it the flow is hidden in group settings, and a
# trigger that somehow fires is refused.
Feature.enable(:duo_mr_risk_classification)

# Gates the "merge request created" event for every flow. Without it only the
# draft-to-ready path fires, so a merge request that opens ready triggers nothing.
Feature.enable(:merge_request_create_flow_trigger)
```

1. Turn the flow on for the top-level group. Go to the group, then **Settings > GitLab Duo > Change configuration**. Under **Flow execution**, select **Allow flow execution** and **Allow foundational flows**, select **Risk Classification**, then **Save changes**.

1. Turn it on for the project. Go to the project, then **Settings > General**, expand **GitLab Duo**, turn on **GitLab Duo**, **Allow flow execution** and **Allow foundational flows**, then **Save changes**.

1. Confirm the triggers came with it. Go to **Automate > Triggers** in the project. Risk Classification has a trigger listing the merge request and merge request ready events, created for you when the flow was turned on. That is the point of this MR: enabling the flow is the only switch, where before nothing started a classification at all.

1. Open a merge request, or mark an existing draft as ready. Then go to **Automate > Agent sessions**: a Risk Classification session appears for it.

1. Confirm `before_start` recorded the run, which is what the widget will read to tell "running" from "never ran":

   ```ruby
   mr = MergeRequest.last

   mr.risk_assessment.status     # => "pending"
   mr.risk_assessment.diff_sha   # => the merge request head SHA
   mr.risk_assessment.score      # => nil, nothing scores it yet
   ```

1. **Expect the session to fail from here, on this branch.** The agent platform config asks for inputs this branch does not send, so the run stops at input validation:

   ```
   input 'risk_classification' does not match specified schema: 'merge_request_iid' is a required property
   ```

   That is the half in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254877, paired with https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/modelops/applied-ml/code-suggestions/ai-assist/-/merge_requests/6872. Check out all three and the run reaches its submit step instead. What this MR is responsible for is everything up to that point: the trigger fired, a session started, and the record is in place.

1. Confirm a flow that declares no callbacks is unaffected, so this changes nothing for every other flow:

   ```ruby
   Ai::Catalog::FoundationalFlow.code_review_v1.run_before_start(resource: MergeRequest.last)
   # => nil
   ```

title: Reduce work items list query complexity for anonymous users
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

This MR brings the work items list query (specifically `getWorkItemsFullEE`) under the **unauthenticated** complexity limit, this is a follow-up of https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/253748.

### Problem

We have following query complexity limits in place for various user types:

- `root` - 300
- Regular users - 250
- Anonymous users - 200

With `work_item_features_field` enabled globally, if an anonymous user would visit a work items list, it would open fine as long as page size is `20` or `50`, but the moment they go to page size `100`, the `getWorkItemsFullEE` query would fail as the total complexity of that query became `240`, thus breaching the limit of `200` for anonymous users. The listing page still loaded and showed work items, but it missed the additional metadata that is fetched via `getWorkItemsFullEE` and user would see a failure banner on the page. For logged in users, this never became an issue as query stayed under `250`.

### Fix

Work Items list currently fires two queries in parallel; `getWorkItemsSlimEE` and `getWorkItemsFullEE`, and we were duplicating the fields in _full_ query, even the ones that we already fetched in _slim_ query, in this MR, we've removed those duplicates, resulting in much smaller complexity. And this is fine because Apollo would merge the results when queries are complete so no fields are lost.

### Implementation notes

- Deduplicated `get_work_items_full.query.graphql` (CE and EE) so it no longer includes fields like `iid`, `author`, `createdAt`, and `webUrl` that `get_work_items_slim.query.graphql` already fetches; this is the change that brings the query under the complexity cap.
- Updated `combineWorkItemLists` in `app/assets/javascripts/work_items/utils.js` to spread the _slim_ item response on top of _full_ item.
- Added the missing `@skip(if: $useWorkItemFeatures)` directive to the EE slim query's `widgets(onlyTypes: [LABELS])` selection, matching CE, since without it EE was loading labels twice on both `widgets[]` and `features` sub-trees.
- Fixed three MSW test suites that assumed slim's fields were a subset of full's: `views_spec.js` and `preferences_spec.js` now look up work items by `title` in the slim fixture instead of full, and we added a real `get_work_items_slim_closed` fixture instead of aliasing the full closed one.
