title: Gate CVS advisory scanner findings on the scanning license
description:
## What

Gate the public continuous-vulnerability-scanning (CVS) advisory scanner, `Gitlab::VulnerabilityScanning::AdvisoryScanner`, on the per-project scanning licensed feature. CVS findings are now only created for Ultimate-eligible projects.

## Why

`AdvisoryScanner#cvs_enabled_for_project?` previously checked only the per-project CVS setting (`cvs_for_dependency_scanning_enabled` / `cvs_for_container_scanning_enabled`), which defaults on. This allowed any project with the setting enabled to receive CVS findings regardless of license tier. CVS findings are Ultimate-only, so the license check was missing.

## Behaviour

- **Ultimate projects**: no change. The licensed feature is available, so the gate passes.
- **Non-Ultimate projects**: will no longer receive CVS findings from this path. Per the Ultimate-only intent of CVS, they should not have been receiving them; this is a correctness fix.
- This path is not behind a feature flag and is live default-on, so the behaviour change ships immediately. A feature flag could be added if the CVS owners prefer a gradual rollout. A changelog entry (type: fixed) is included.

## Related

- Companion to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/249075 (malware CVS gate)

`ee/spec/lib/gitlab/vulnerability_scanning/advisory_scanner_spec.rb` now stubs `dependency_scanning` and `container_scanning` availability. description:
## What does this MR do and why?

**Commit 1: fix misspelled table name**

- `ee/app/workers/security/scans/ingest_reports_worker.rb`: `vulnerability_occurences` → `vulnerability_occurrences`.
- Only `AutovacuumActiveOnTable` reads that table list, so the typo meant it always checked a table that doesn't exist.
- Spec coverage added for the corrected name.

**Commit 2: gate `Sbom::IngestReportsWorker` on database health**

- Adds `defer_on_database_health_signal :gitlab_sec, [:sbom_occurrences], 1.minute`, behind flag `defer_sbom_ingest_reports_on_database_health` (type `gitlab_com_derisk`, default disabled).
- Default-off: no behaviour change until enabled.
- Worker writes to the sec database inline with no `concurrency_limit`; sibling workers are already gated.
- Production log analysis into sec-database WAL generation pressure identified `Sbom::IngestReportsWorker` as a significant contributor; see References for supporting evidence.
- Spec coverage added.
- Low risk: no migrations, no user-facing change.

## References

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/628675
- https://runbooks.gitlab.com/patroni/primary_db_node_wal_generation_saturation/

All from the production investigation, window `2026-09-10 22:00` to `2026-09-11 00:00` UTC.

**Sec DB writes per job, p99 by worker class.** `Sbom::IngestReportsWorker` reaches 38,896 writes in a single job at 22:09. The next-highest worker in the same bucket is `Security::StoreSecurityReportsByProjectWorker` at 587.

![shot2](/uploads/41fe35bd55d3123c03a3ee897ca58800/shot2.png)

**`patroni-sec` WAL generation saturation.** Peaks at 65.9% at 22:40, against a 70% soft SLO and a 90% hard SLO. The 99th percentile for the week is 42.9%.

## How to set up and validate locally

   ```ruby

   ```
1. Run the specs:
   ```shell
   bundle exec rspec ee/spec/workers/sbom/ingest_reports_worker_spec.rb ee/spec/workers/security/scans/ingest_reports_worker_spec.rb
   ```

<details>
<summary>Notes for reviewers: pre-existing quirks in the deferral mechanism</summary>

**Autovacuum indicator doesn't see the sec connection.** `AutovacuumActiveOnTable` is the only indicator that reads the `tables:` list; it queries via `PostgresAutovacuumActivity`, a `SharedModel`. `SkipJobs` never wraps it in `SharedModel.using_connection`, unlike `app/workers/database/batched_background_migration/execution_worker.rb:52`, so it evaluates against main for every `:gitlab_sec` worker. The table-name fix here doesn't activate anything today; SBOM gating relies on the cluster-wide `WalRate` indicator instead. A fix belongs in `SkipJobs`, out of scope here.

**Deduplication during deferral.** `SkipJobs` runs after `DuplicateJobs::Server`, so deferring releases the `until_executed` key, and re-enqueued deferred jobs skip deduplication. A repeat event for the same `pipeline_id` can enqueue a second job. Bounded in practice.

</details>

title: Make origin-anchored Xd granularity the default for all aggregation engines
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

DAP Impact dashboards need to compare rolling periods, like the last 30 days versus the previous 30 days, for any metric. Time bucketing previously only understood calendar periods (daily, weekly, monthly), so a rolling comparison meant two separate requests stitched together, which is slower and easier to get wrong.

This MR makes fixed-day, origin-anchored granularity a built-in default for every aggregation engine instead of something each engine has to opt into. Date bucket dimensions now accept `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, or a fixed number of days such as `30d` (from `1d` to `399d`), plus an optional `origin` timestamp. With a fixed-day granularity and an origin, buckets start at that origin and repeat every N days, so a single request returns the previous and current period side by side. Combining `origin` with a calendar granularity is rejected as invalid, and calendar granularities behave exactly as before.

Notes for reviewers:

- This surfaces in GraphQL as `granularity` and `origin` arguments on the date dimension fields of all aggregation response types (AgentPlatformSessions, Contributions, Deployments, DuoWorkflows, MergeRequests, Pipelines, CodeSuggestions, AiUsageEvents). The GraphQL reference docs and introspection result are regenerated.
- Because the dimension now has two default parameters, internal result column aliases include the parameter name (for example `created_at_monthly` becomes `created_at_granularity_monthly`). This accounts for most of the spec churn and has no effect on the GraphQL API, since clients choose their own field aliases.

Related to #609138

## References

- Issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/609138
- Epic: https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/23225

## Screenshots or screen recordings

Not applicable: backend and GraphQL API change only.

## How to set up and validate locally

1. Ensure ClickHouse is running in GDK.
1. Enable the feature flag in a Rails console: `Feature.enable(:dap_impact_v1)`.
1. Make sure there is some Duo Workflow / agent session data for a group you can query.
1. Run the following GraphQL query against that group:

   ```graphql
   query {
     group(fullPath: "gitlab-org") {
       analytics {
         duoWorkflows {
           aggregated(orderBy: [{ identifier: "createdAt", direction: ASC, parameters: { granularity: "30d", origin: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" } }]) {
             nodes {
               dimensions { period: createdAt(granularity: "30d", origin: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z") }
               totalCount
               usersCount
             }
           }
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```

   Expect one node per 30-day window starting at the origin, with the previous and current window both present in the same response.
1. Confirm that combining `granularity: "monthly"` with an `origin` returns a validation error.
1. Confirm that plain `granularity: "monthly"` (no origin) still works as before.
1. Run the relevant specs:

   ```shell
   bin/rspec spec/lib/gitlab/database/aggregation/click_house/date_bucket_dimension_spec.rb ee/spec/requests/api/graphql/analytics/duo_workflows_spec.rb
   ```

## What does this MR do and why?

- Moves all security_orchestration jest integration specs from `ee/spec/frontend_integration/` to `ee/spec/frontend/security_orchestration/integration/`, keeping the `policies_list/` and `policy_editor/` subtree. 35 of the 39 files are pure renames.
- Frontend Testing is deleting the `spec/frontend_integration` harness (MirageJS, `jest.config.integration.js`, `jest-integration` job) in favour of a single jest + MSW integration story. These specs never used that harness — they are `mountExtended` + `createMockApollo` specs — so they move unchanged rather than being rewritten onto MSW.
- **The old home had no vue3 job**, so the move puts these specs under `jest vue3` for the first time. Four things had to be fixed for them to pass there:
  - `App` mounts now get an `apolloProvider`. Without one, `ScopeSection.showLoader` reads `this.$apollo.queries` off an undefined `$apollo`. The shared provider (`policy_editor/apollo_util.js`, moved up from `pipeline_execution/`) also carries the security configuration resolvers/typePolicies the DAST profile selector needs, and default handlers for the SPP linked-items query so `ScopeSection` renders its normal state rather than its error branch.
  - Three specs mock the policy schema `GET` the YAML editor issues on mount, via a shared `mockPolicySchemaRequest`. The old harness swapped in a real HTTP adapter so MirageJS answered it; `spec/frontend` fails unmocked requests instead.
  - `override_action_spec` emitted `select` through a nested `findComponent` lookup that finds nothing in VTU 2, since the test id sits on the listbox itself.

title: Send fully qualified ref in commits list query
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Fixes #628204

When a branch and a tag share the same name, the Vue commits list sent the bare ref name to the GraphQL commits query. Git resolves bare names with `refs/tags/*` taking precedence over `refs/heads/*`, so the page showed the tag's history even when the URL had `?ref_type=heads` or the user picked the branch from the disambiguation popup.

This MR adds a `qualifiedRef` computed that prefixes the ref with `refs/<type>/` when the ref type is known (`heads` or `tags`), so an explicit ref type always wins. Commit SHAs have no ref type and are sent unchanged. `pipelineRef` stays bare because pipelines are matched on their stored bare ref name.

Refs containing slashes (e.g. `feature/dev`) pass through untouched, producing `refs/heads/feature/dev`.

title: Add the Artifact registry namespace details read
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

The create route performs no Artifact Registry read of its own, so it has nowhere to obtain the `create_repository` verdict that gates its controls. `Client#namespace_details` reads `GET /api/v1/:slug/namespace` as the current user, the one read this slice adds to any page, and returns a `NamespaceDetails` value object carrying slug, created_at, and the namespace-scope verdicts.

The read is per-user with a bearer token, not the service credential, because the verdicts describe what this caller may attempt and the service credential has no caller. `include_permissions` defaults to false and sends the query parameter only when true. The exposed permissions keep the same three states the repository reads use: nil when not requested, absent when requested but not served, populated otherwise. A 404 returns nil and is logged, mirroring the repository list read, because a slug that stopped resolving is a drift worth diagnosing.

`NamespaceDetails` is a new object rather than a permissions reader on `Namespace`, because `Namespace` is built from a different read with different required keys. Its permissions argument is positional like `Repository`'s, so the two stay consistent.

Everything is dark behind the default-off `artifact_registry_ui` feature flag. There is no changelog entry for that reason.

title: Prevent submodule race conditions with expected_old_oid check
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Fixes: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/384021

This MR adds `expected_old_oid` support to `UserUpdateSubmodule` to protect against race conditions when multiple users try updating the same submodule ref. It ensures the current SHA matches the expected one before applying the update.

## How to set up and validate locally

I created a dummy submodule repo dummy-submodule and added it to the flightjs/Flight project. Then I simulated a series of updates using both the Rails console and the CLI to test different race condition scenarios.

#### Rails Console Testing:

---

* Loaded the project, repo and user

```
project = Project.find_by_full_path('flightjs/Flight')
repo = project.repository
user = User.find_by_username('root')
```

* **Initial set to SHA A (User A)**

```
repo.gitaly_operation_client.user_update_submodule(
  user: user,
  submodule: 'dummy-submodule',
  commit_sha: '650e8445...', # SHA A
  branch: 'master',
  message: 'User A sets submodule to SHA A',
  expected_old_oid: ''
)
```

* **Force set to SHA C (CLI overwrite)**

```
repo.gitaly_operation_client.user_update_submodule(
  user: user,
  submodule: 'dummy-submodule',
  commit_sha: 'c993ede2...', # SHA C
  branch: 'master',
  message: 'CLI: force update to SHA C',
  expected_old_oid: ''
)
```

* **User B tries setting SHA B expecting stale SHA A – should fail**

```
repo.update_submodule(
  user: user,
  submodule: 'dummy-submodule',
  commit_sha: '527bb126...', # SHA B
  branch: 'master',
  message: 'User B tries update with stale expected_old_oid',
  expected_old_oid: '650e8445...' # stale
)
# ❌ Fails with:
# ValidationError: Submodule was updated by someone else. Please try again.
```

* **Reset pointer to fresh SHA**

```
repo.gitaly_operation_client.user_update_submodule(
  user: user,
  submodule: 'dummy-submodule',
  commit_sha: '1e72ec9f...', # fresh commit
  branch: 'master',
  message: 'Reset Flight to fresh SHA',
  expected_old_oid: ''
)
# ✅ Pass
```

* **Valid update with matching expected SHA**

```
repo.update_submodule(
  user: user,
  submodule: 'dummy-submodule',
  commit_sha: '54fc54e0...', # Race-safe commit
  branch: 'master',
  message: 'Race-safe update: fresh expected SHA',
  expected_old_oid: '1e72ec9f...'
)
# ✅ Pass
```

* **Invalid update with stale expected SHA – should fail**

```
repo.update_submodule(
  user: user,
  submodule: 'dummy-submodule',
  commit_sha: '527bb126...',
  branch: 'master',
  message: 'Stale update attempt – should fail',
  expected_old_oid: '1e72ec9f...'
)
# ❌ Fails with:
# ValidationError: Submodule was updated by someone else. Please try again.
```

**Test Scenarios Verified in Rails Console**

| **Case** | **Expected Result** |
|----------|---------------------|
| Initial set to SHA A | ✅ Pass |
| Force set to SHA C (no expected SHA) | ✅ Pass |
| User B tries to update to SHA B expecting SHA A | ❌ Fails (race detected) |
| Reset pointer to fresh SHA | ✅ Pass |
| Valid update with matching expected SHA | ✅ Pass |
| Invalid update with stale expected SHA | :x: Fails |


#### **CLI Testing:**

---

```
curl --request PUT "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v4/projects/7/repository/submodules/dummy-submodule" \
  --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-raw '{
    "submodule": "dummy-submodule",
    "branch": "master",
    "commit_sha": "ff859e34...",
    "commit_message": "Test submodule update with expected_old_oid",
    "expected_old_oid": "60fae8ab..." # stale SHA
  }'
```

Failed with:

```
{"message":"Submodule was updated by someone else. Please try again."}
```

description:
Adds the `vue3_migrate_clusters` feature flag and a `vue3_migration.yml` for 13
Kubernetes cluster page entrypoints. This opts them into the Vue 3 migration
with Option 1. The bundler builds both a Vue 2 and a Vue 3 chunk. Rails serves
the Vue 3 chunk only when the flag is on. The flag is default-off.

## Scope

This covers 13 of the 16 cluster entrypoints. The three `*/clusters/destroy`
bundles are excluded. That action only redirects and never renders HTML, so
those bundles can never load. A companion merge request removes them.

Most of these pages sit behind the `certificate_based_clusters` ops flag, which
defaults to off. Every `admin/clusters` page returns 404 while it is off. The
exception is the agent tab on `*/clusters/index`, which always renders and is
linked from three sidebars. Grouping the deprecated pages under the same flag
stops them being stranded on Vue 2 when the certificate flag is removed.

`~/clusters/clusters_bundle.js:104` mounts with the raw `new Vue({ el, ... })`

invisible. It needs a manual check before the flag is ramped.

title: Migrate policy store policy delete to GraphQL
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Migrates the policy store detail page's policy delete from the REST endpoint to the `governPolicyDelete` GraphQL mutation, called directly from the detail component via `this.$apollo.mutate` (the detail app gains an `apolloProvider` for this). The store's rejection message is now surfaced in the delete alert instead of only a generic message. The `deletePolicy` wrapper is removed from `policies.js` along with the now-unused `Api.deletePolicyStorePolicy` REST method.

Closes #617793.

**REST wrapper audit**

- `Api.deletePolicyStorePolicy` was the last consumer of the REST delete and is removed together with its spec; the `deletePolicy` wrapper in `policies.js` is removed entirely since the component now calls the mutation itself (verified by grep — no references remain).
- `fetchPolicies` and `updatePolicy` still call REST and still have consumers (list page, status toggle) — they belong to the remaining migration issues.
- The now-unused `getPolicyStorePolicy` REST method is left for the open fetch-migration MR !252321 to clean up.

### Notes for reviewers

- Policy store ids are plain `Int` at the GraphQL boundary, not GlobalIDs — the `Number(policyId)` cast follows the convention established in !250240 and continued in !251612 (ids are frozen gem value objects, not ActiveRecord models, so no GlobalID exists; REST takes the same plain integer).
- The only payload error the backend can currently return for delete is the store's `Policy was not found` constant, which is not externalized for translation. Surfacing it follows the acceptance criteria and matches how the create flow already surfaces store messages; store-message translation is a store-side concern. Any other failure (experiment gate, unmapped reasons) arrives as a top-level GraphQL error and keeps the translated generic alert.
- An adversarial review of the first revision (wrapper-based) returned "pass with findings" (verbatim verdict). The mutation call then moved from a `policies.js` wrapper into the component at the author's direction; error semantics, variables, and spec coverage carried over unchanged. Non-blocking findings kept as follow-ups: the payload destructure assumes a non-null payload (safe under Apollo's default `errorPolicy: 'none'`, and consistent with `createPolicy`); Sentry still captures not-found deletes (pre-existing behavior); after a not-found the page still renders the deleted policy (pre-existing under REST).

## References

- Issue: #617793 (confidential)
- Approved plan: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/617793#note_3754638849
- Epic: &22542
- Related: !252321 — adds the identical `apolloProvider` wiring to `detail.js`; whichever merges second rebases trivially
- Backend mutation (already merged): `ee/app/graphql/mutations/govern/policy_delete.rb`

## Screenshots or screen recordings

No visual changes. The delete flow keeps the same confirmation modal and button; only the failure alert can now carry the store's message instead of always the generic copy.

## How to set up and validate locally

1. Enable the policy store experiment for an organization (GDK): in `rails console`, ensure `organization.policy_store_experiment_active?` returns `true` for your organization, and sign in as a user with the `delete_govern_policy` ability (instance admin / organization owner).
2. Create a policy via the wizard at `/-/organizations/<organization_path>/security/policy_store/new`.
3. Open the policy's detail page at `/-/organizations/<organization_path>/security/policy_store/<id>` and click **Delete**, then confirm.
4. Expected: the network tab shows a `governPolicyDelete` GraphQL request (no `DELETE /api/v4/organizations/:id/security/policy_store/:policy_id` call), and the browser returns to the policy list.
5. Delete the same policy again from a second tab opened beforehand: the alert shows the store's message (`Policy was not found`) instead of the generic copy.

- the new mutation document validated against `tmp/tests/graphql/gitlab_schema.graphql` with the `graphql` package (`document valid`)

title: Document Secrets Manager secret count limits
description:
## What does this MR do?

GitLab Secrets Manager enforces a per-project secret count limit (default 100) and a per-group secret count limit (default 500), but until now these limits were only documented in the Application Settings API reference. Users who hit the cap had no user-facing page explaining what happened or how to raise it. This MR adds that documentation in two places.

- Adds a "Secret limits" section to `doc/ci/secrets/secrets_manager/_index.md`, listing the per-project count limit (100), per-group count limit (500), and secret value size limit (10 KB), and noting that an administrator must raise the count limits.
- Adds a "Secrets Manager limits" section to `doc/administration/instance_limits.md`, with a table of the same three limits and whether each is configurable.
- Both new sections warn that setting `project_secrets_limit` or `group_secrets_limit` to `0` removes the limit entirely, allowing unlimited secret creation, which can exhaust instance resources.
- Cross-links the two pages to each other and to the Application Settings API reference.
- No change was needed in `doc/api/settings.md`, since it already documents both settings and the `0` behavior.

title: Analyze newly created partitions bypassing the analyze interval
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

The partition manager only ANALYZEs a partitioned table on a throttled interval, and that throttle checks the oldest partition's last-analyze timestamp. A brand-new partition can therefore serve queries with zero planner statistics until the interval elapses, letting the planner pick pathological plans — this is what caused INC-13566, where a fresh `security_findings` partition fell back to a massive parallel sequential scan.

The fix runs the throttled whole-table ANALYZE first (its recurse already covers every partition), and when the throttle skips it, runs `ANALYZE (SKIP_LOCKED)` directly on each newly created partition after the create/attach transaction commits — so the planner has real statistics from the partition's first query either way.

Resolves https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/627248.

## How to set up and validate locally

1. `bin/rspec spec/lib/gitlab/database/partitioning/partition_manager_spec.rb`
1. All examples pass; the context "when a partition is created within the analyze interval" shows the newly created partition gets analyzed directly while the whole-table ANALYZE stays throttled.

<details>
<summary>Supporting evidence</summary>

- Scope: the per-partition ANALYZE only runs for models whose partitioning strategy sets `analyze_interval` — same opt-in as the existing whole-table ANALYZE. https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/624175 and https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/252300 add a default `analyze_interval` per strategy; once both land, every partitioned model is covered.
- Flag coordination: gated behind the same ops kill-switch `analyze_partitioned_tables_on_rotation` (default enabled) as https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/252300. The flag YAML here is scoped to what this MR guards; whichever MR merges second rebases, drops the duplicate file, and broadens the description once both paths share the gate.
- Lock/cost: the ANALYZE runs after the `with_lock_retries` create/attach transaction commits, so it doesn't extend the SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock window. The partition is empty at this point, so the ANALYZE costs milliseconds. `SKIP_LOCKED` skips it if another process holds a conflicting lock — now detected via `pg_class.reltuples` and logged as a warning.
- Failure isolation: ANALYZE errors are rescued per path and logged as "Failed to run ANALYZE on created partitions" / "Failed to run ANALYZE on partitioned table", instead of surfacing under the pre-existing (and by then misleading) "Failed to create / detach partition(s)" message, since creation has already committed. A whole-table ANALYZE failure still falls back to the per-partition pass.
- Verification: RuboCop clean on both changed files. `bin/rspec spec/lib/gitlab/database/partitioning/partition_manager_spec.rb` → 55 examples, 0 failures, 1 pending (pre-existing environment-conditional skip). `bin/rspec spec/lib/gitlab/database/partitioning_spec.rb` → 24 examples, 0 failures, 1 pending. The new spec contexts create a real partition while the throttle is satisfied and assert it receives `ANALYZE (SKIP_LOCKED)` and real statistics (`pg_class.reltuples >= 0`; `-1` means never analyzed), plus coverage for the no-duplicate ordering, the whole-table-failure fallback, and the SKIP_LOCKED warning.
- Related: production incident INC-13566. An earlier mitigation, https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/252297, set `analyze_interval: 1.day` on `Security::Finding` — that shrinks the stats-less window but doesn't close it.

</details>

title: Resolve instance-level SSH CAs in /internal/authorized_certs
description:
<!--
**Not ready yet?** Add `[ci skip]` to your MR title to skip the pipeline and save CI resources. 
It's a small habit that makes a big difference for our shared compute budget and overall system load. 
Every pipeline counts! 🙌
-->

## What does this MR do and why?

Resolve instance-level SSH CAs in /internal/authorized_certs

Update endpoint to handle instance level ssh certificates.

It checks group level certificates and falls back to the instance service when no group CA matches the fingerprint.

When neither service finds a matching certificate the error comes from the scope that matched the fingerprint. Both find services return semantic reasons so the endpoint can tell a missing certificate from a denial, and the endpoint maps those reasons to HTTP statuses.
Group-only resolution is unaffected: the group error still wins whenever a group CA claimed the fingerprint.

Every group failure still falls through to the instance scope, including a member who is not an enterprise user of the group and a
group that is not licensed for ssh_certificates.

Related to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/611274

## How to set up and validate locally

1. Confirm the GDK instance is not configured as SaaS. The feature is not available on GitLab.com.
1. Enable the flag in the Rails console:
   ```ruby
   Feature.enable(:instance_ssh_certificates)
   ```
1. Create an instance CA in the Rails console. The fingerprint is derived from the key:
   ```ruby
   InstanceSshCertificate.create!(title: 'Test CA', key: File.read('/path/to/ca_key.pub'))
   ```
1. The endpoint requires a GitLab Shell JWT, so exercise it through the request specs:
   ```shell
   bundle exec rspec ee/spec/requests/api/internal/base_spec.rb -e "GET /internal/authorized_certs"
   ```
1. Confirm an instance match returns `{"success":true,"instance":true,"username":"..."}` with no `namespace` key.
1. Register a group CA for the same fingerprint and confirm the group match wins, and that a group denial still falls through to the instance CA.

title: Add save_vulnerability MCP Server tool
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Implements the `save_vulnerability` MCP Server tool for the Duo Agent Platform, covering 5 write operations on GitLab vulnerabilities in a single consolidated tool:

- **dismiss** - mark a vulnerability as dismissed, with optional comment and dismissal reason
- **confirm** - mark a vulnerability as confirmed
- **revert_to_detected** - revert a vulnerability's state back to detected
- **update_severity** - override the severity with a required comment
- **create_issue** - create a new issue linked to the vulnerability (requires project_full_path)

Follows the SavePipelineTool multi-operation pattern with an OPERATIONS constant hash and action-dispatched build_variables.

Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/613026

## References

- Issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/613026
- Reference implementation (read-side): https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/251243

## How to set up and validate locally

### Prerequisites
- GitLab EE instance running locally (GDK)
- A project with vulnerabilities (run a SAST scan or seed vulnerability data)
- A personal access token with `api` scope

### Direct API test with curl

1. List tools to confirm registration
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v4/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-pat>' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```
Confirm 'save_vulnerability' appears in the response with readOnlyHint: false, destructiveHint: false

2. Get a vulnerability ID to test with

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v4/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-pat>' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list_vulnerabilities","arguments":{"project_full_path":"<namespace/project>","first":5}}}'
```
Note a vulnerability ID from the response (just the numeric part, e.g., "123")

3. Test confirm action

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v4/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-pat>' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"save_vulnerability","arguments":{"action":"confirm","vulnerability_id":"<numeric-id>","comment":"Verified this is real"}}}'
```
Expected: Returns vulnerability with state: "confirmed"

4. Test dismiss action with reason
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v4/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-pat>' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"save_vulnerability","arguments":{"action":"dismiss","vulnerability_id":"<numeric-id>","dismissal_reason":"FALSE_POSITIVE","comment":"Not a real issue"}}}'
```
 Expected: Returns vulnerability with state: "dismissed"
Valid dismissal reasons: ACCEPTABLE_RISK, FALSE_POSITIVE, MITIGATING_CONTROL, USED_IN_TESTS, NOT_APPLICABLE

5. Test revert_to_detected action
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v4/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-pat>' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"save_vulnerability","arguments":{"action":"revert_to_detected","vulnerability_id":"<numeric-id>"}}}'
```
Expected: Returns vulnerability with state: "detected"

6. Test update_severity action (comment is required)
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v4/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-pat>' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"save_vulnerability","arguments":{"action":"update_severity","vulnerability_id":"<numeric-id>","severity":"CRITICAL","comment":"Elevating based on impact"}}}'
```
Expected: Returns vulnerability with severity: "CRITICAL"
Valid severities: INFO, UNKNOWN, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL

7. Test create_issue action (project_full_path is required)
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v4/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-pat>' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"save_vulnerability","arguments":{"action":"create_issue","vulnerability_id":"<numeric-id>","project_full_path":"<namespace/project>"}}}'
```
Expected: Creates a new issue linked to the vulnerability

8. Test error case - non-existent vulnerability
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v4/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <your-pat>' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":8,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"save_vulnerability","arguments":{"action":"confirm","vulnerability_id":"999999"}}}'
```

title: Add application setting to block JWT for reclaimed project paths
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Adds an application setting `block_jwt_for_reclaimed_paths` (default: `true`) that allows administrators of self-managed and Dedicated instances to disable the security restriction introduced in GitLab 19.1 that blocks CI/CD JWT/OIDC token generation for projects that have reclaimed a previously used namespace path.

The restriction is **on by default** for all instance types. This setting gives Dedicated customers a supported path to unblock legitimate CI/CD pipelines that are affected by the fix for https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/600358, without weakening the default security posture.

**Changes:**
- New boolean key `block_jwt_for_reclaimed_paths` (default: `true`) in the `ci_cd_settings` JSONB column — no DB migration needed
- JSON schema updated to allow the new key
- `JwtV2#verify_path_not_burned!` is a no-op when the setting is `false`
- `Ci::RegisterJobService#id_token_burned_project_path?` returns `false` when the setting is `false`
- Admin Area UI toggle in the CI/CD settings section (hidden on GitLab.com)
- API write path blocked on GitLab.com (see below)
- On GitLab.com the restriction is hardcoded to `true` regardless of the stored value (see below)
- Documentation for the API and Admin Area settings page
- Specs covering default value, bypass behavior, and SaaS enforcement

**Why EE code is involved despite the setting being available in CE**

The setting definition, enforcement logic, Admin UI, and API write parameter are all in CE (`app/models/`, `lib/`, `app/views/`, `lib/api/helpers/settings_helpers.rb`). CE self-managed instances get full read/write access through these code paths with no changes needed.

The EE additions serve two purposes:

- **Hardcoding enforcement on GitLab.com** — `ee/app/models/ee/application_setting.rb` overrides `block_jwt_for_reclaimed_paths` to always return `true` when `Gitlab::Saas.feature_available?(:gitlab_com_subscriptions)`, regardless of the stored value. Both CE enforcement points read this accessor, so no changes are needed there.
- **Blocking writes on GitLab.com** — `ee/lib/ee/api/settings.rb` strips the attribute in `filter_attributes_using_license` using `Gitlab::Saas.feature_available?(:gitlab_com_subscriptions)`, preventing a GitLab.com admin from changing it via the API even if they know the attribute name.

**Known limitation — field appears in GitLab.com GET response**

The CE entity exposes all `visible_attributes` unconditionally via `expose(*exposed_attributes)`. There is no clean way for the EE module to suppress a field already registered by the CE entity without either breaking CE read/write parity or relying on undocumented Grape::Entity duplicate-expose behaviour. Since:

- the accessor always returns `true` on GitLab.com regardless of the stored value,
- writes are already blocked by `filter_attributes_using_license`, and
- the Admin UI hides the toggle via `unless Gitlab.com?`,

the field appearing in the GitLab.com GET response is an accepted known limitation with no security impact.

## References

- Work item: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/623356
- Original security fix: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/600358
- Original MR: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/security/gitlab/-/merge_requests/6229
- Original commit in canonical: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/security/gitlab/-/commit/11ecdab72b147e25a85b7419c37df64045c44f4f

## Screenshots or screen recordings

| Before | After  |
| ------ | ------ |
| No toggle available | See https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254058#note_3820924623 |

## How to set up and validate locally

1. In the Admin area, go to **Settings > CI/CD** and expand **Continuous Integration and Deployment**.
1. Verify the new **Block JWT generation in reclaimed project paths** checkbox is visible and checked by default.
1. In rails console, create a burned project route and verify the setting bypasses the check:
   ```ruby
   # With setting enabled (default), JWT minting raises for burned paths
   ApplicationSetting.current.block_jwt_for_reclaimed_paths # => true

   # Disable the setting
   ApplicationSetting.current.update!(block_jwt_for_reclaimed_paths: false)

   # Now JWT minting succeeds even for burned paths
   ```

title: fix(geo): Clear stale verification_failure on pending/succeeded transitions
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Clears stale Geo verification failure fields when verification is reset to pending or moves to succeeded, including when the update is made through a stale in-memory copy.

`verification_failure = nil` is a dirty-tracking no-op when the in-memory value is already `nil`. If another process has since written a failure message, the `UPDATE` omits the column and the database retains that message. A shared `clear_verification_failure!` helper forces the column into the update before assigning `nil`. The `VerifiableRegistry` override does the same for `checksum_mismatch` and `verification_checksum_mismatched`.

The full failure-field cleanup also forces `verification_retry_count` and `verification_retry_at` into the update. A stale copy can already hold `0`/`nil` while another process has recorded retry history; ordinary assignments would otherwise leave that history in the database.

Cleanup is skipped on pending-to-pending loopback transitions (`transition.loopback?`), so a clean pending self-transition stays a no-op and issues no `UPDATE`. A stale pending copy therefore loses to a concurrent failure write; every other transition in this MR changes `verification_state`, so an `UPDATE` happens anyway and the forced-dirty columns cost nothing extra.

Failed/disabled-to-pending transitions continue to preserve retry history and progressive backoff.

## References

- Closes #627715.
- Related: !253429 and #601974.

No UI changes.

The MR adds twelve regression examples across the concern spec and shared registry examples. They use separately loaded copies and assert persisted results after reloading, covering stale failure messages, checksum mismatches, and retry fields. Stale pending-to-pending examples assert the stale writer loses to a concurrent failure, and a `QueryRecorder` example asserts a clean pending-to-pending transition issues no `UPDATE`. Retry-reset examples load the stale copy with persisted `0`/`nil` retry fields so normal dirty tracking cannot mask the defect. title: Add Policy Store RegoValidator and depend on gitlab-glaz
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

A Policy Store policy whose Rego does not parse used to save cleanly, read as enforcing, and only fail at evaluation time where nobody sees the error. This MR introduces the validator that closes that gap; a following MR wires it into the repository port.

`Gitlab::PolicyStore::RegoValidator` parses a Rego program through `Gitlab::Glaz::GovernPolicyEngine#validate` and raises `Gitlab::PolicyStore::ValidationError` with the parser's message and location (e.g. `rules[0] is invalid: ... (at 3:8)`). The engine's `validate` is parse-only: unsafe variables, recursion, unknown builtins, and arity errors pass it and only fail at evaluation. Each reported message is capped at 1000 bytes in case the engine echoes offending source.

Failure handling is fail-closed: an engine fault, a malformed engine result (including `valid: false` with no errors), or any unexpected error raises `Gitlab::PolicyStore::EngineError` (a `ValidationError` subclass), so the save is refused rather than stored unvalidated and the caller gets a domain error — a 400, not a 500. The original exception is kept as `cause`. Invalid UTF-8, whether tagged UTF-8 or binary, raises `ValidationError`.

This adds `gitlab-glaz` as the gem's runtime dependency and bumps the required Ruby to `>= 3.3` to match [gitlab-glaz's](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ruby/gems/gitlab-glaz/-/blob/main/gitlab-glaz.gemspec#L14) own constraint. 

## Stacked with

Follow-up: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254250 targets this branch and wires `RegoValidator` into the repository port (`Ports::PolicyRepository`). It carries the shared contract examples, the EE repository and API specs, and the `doc/api/policy_store.md` update. Nothing in this MR calls the validator yet, so no user-facing behavior changes until that MR merges.

## How to test

```ruby
Gitlab::PolicyStore::RegoValidator.validate!(:policy_rego, "package governance\n\nallow := true\n")
# => true

Gitlab::PolicyStore::RegoValidator.validate!("rules[0]", "package governance\n\nallow if {\n")
# => Gitlab::PolicyStore::ValidationError: rules[0] is invalid: error: expecting expression (at 4:1)
```

End-to-end behavior (a 400 from the policies API for a `custom` rule or authored `scope_rego` that does not parse) is exercised by the follow-up MR's test plan: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254250.

- Issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/618556
- gitlab-glaz `validate` entry point: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/auth/glaz/-/merge_requests/132

description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Adds the `benchmark-swap` gem to the `development` and `test` groups, and documents it in the
performance guide next to `benchmark-ips` and `benchmark-memory`.

`benchmark-swap` compares two implementations of a method where that method already runs. You keep
the original, add a second implementation next to it with a `_perf` suffix on the name, then call
`Benchmark.swap` with a block. The gem finds the pair by tracing the block with `TracePoint`, swaps
the body in place, and compares both sides with `benchmark-ips`.

The reason to swap in place is that measuring a method on its own answers a different question. A
method lifted into two standalone lambdas can show a speed-up that the caller never feels. When the
swap happens in place, the block calls the public entry point and the measurement covers the whole
call chain. The worked example in the guide shows this: the same change measures 1.61x on
`Security::MergeReportsService#deduplicated_findings` alone, and 1.40x through `execute`. The second
number is the one worth acting on.

`benchmark-ips` is already a dependency, and `benchmark-swap` builds on it. The gem is loaded with
`require: false`, so it costs nothing until you require it from a console.

Disclosure: I wrote this gem. It is MIT licensed, published on RubyGems, and its CI runs the specs
on Ruby 3.2, 3.3 and 3.4. Source: https://github.com/meinac/benchmark-swap

## How to set up and validate locally

Run the following on your GDK/gitlab-monolith root directory;

```sh
curl https://gitlab.com/-/snippets/6052892/raw/main/benchmark-swap.rb -o tmp/benchmark-swap.rb
GITLAB_ROOT=$(pwd) ruby tmp/benchmark-swap.rb
```

title: Handle Zoekt connection errors in aggregations and blob search
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Both commits fix the same root cause: a `::Search::Zoekt::Errors::ClientConnectionError` escaping past the code that is supposed to turn it into a handled search failure. The first commit fixes this for the `aggregations` action; the second fixes a related gap on the blob search path itself.

### 1. Return a 503 from `SearchController#aggregations`

Adds a rescue clause for `::Search::Zoekt::Errors::ClientConnectionError` in the `aggregations` action in `ee/app/controllers/ee/search_controller.rb`. On this error it calls `::Gitlab::ErrorTracking.log_exception`, derives `error_type` from the class name the same way the existing rescue does (yielding `client_connection_error`), and renders `{ error:, error_type: }` with status `:service_unavailable`.

Why:

- The action already treats "search backend unreachable" as a 503 with a structured body, but the existing rescue only lists `::Gitlab::Search::Client::ConnectionError` and `::Gitlab::Search::Client::AuthorizationError`, which are Elasticsearch classes.
- `Search::Zoekt::Errors::ClientConnectionError` descends from a plain `StandardError` with unrelated ancestry, so it escaped the action. `Gitlab::Search::Zoekt::Client` raises it on network errors and on an unparseable JSON body (`ee/lib/gitlab/search/zoekt/client.rb`, around lines 128 and 158).
- Today, an unreachable or slow Zoekt node produces an unhandled exception reported to Sentry as a 500 from `SearchController#aggregations`, which reads like an application bug rather than a downstream dependency being down. One event per `aggregations` request, so it scales with search traffic during an outage.
- The response body uses a fixed message, `Search is currently unavailable. Please try again later.`, rather than `e.message`. The Zoekt error carries the raw transport failure including the node URL, which must not be echoed to the client. The Elasticsearch classes hardcode a safe message on the class itself (`ee/lib/gitlab/search/client.rb`, around lines 62-72); the Zoekt one does not, and giving it one would hide the real cause from logs on the search path.

### 2. Stop the language tally from failing the whole blob search

`Search::Zoekt::SearchResults#known_languages` in `ee/lib/search/zoekt/search_results.rb` now rescues `::Search::Zoekt::Errors::ClientConnectionError` and returns an empty array.

Why:

- `#zoekt_search` already rescues `ClientConnectionError` for the results query and converts it into `@error_message` / `@is_server_error`, surfaced through `failed?` / `server_error?`. But `#zoekt_search_and_wrap` calls `#known_languages` to build the `Search::Zoekt::Cache` key, and that call happens before the block that `#zoekt_search` rescues.
- With the `Unknown` language filter applied and a cold aggregation cache, `#known_languages` issues the language-tally request itself, so the error escapes past the rescue to the caller.
- Who is exposed: `SearchController#count` (chain: `formatted_count('blobs')` then `blobs_and_file_count` then `search_as_found_blob` then `zoekt_search_and_wrap`), and the GraphQL `blobSearch` resolver (`Resolvers::Search::Blob::BlobSearchResolver`), which is what the blob results UI actually calls. Both expect a failed result object, not a raised exception.
- Not exposed: `SearchController#show`, because `multi_match?` is true for scope `blobs` with search type `zoekt`, so `haml_search_results` is skipped and the action runs no Zoekt query. Also not exposed: `SearchController#autocomplete`, because `search_autocomplete_opts` never calls `Gitlab::Search::Zoekt::Client`.
- Also not exposed: the REST Search API (`lib/api/search.rb`) reaches the same `SearchResults#objects` chain, so it has the same shape of exposure in principle, but it doesn't take a `language` parameter, so `known_languages` is never invoked and the tally is never attempted.
- An empty array is the right fallback because it is the case `CodeQueryBuilder#unknown_atom` already handles: without a known-language list the complement cannot be expressed, so the `Unknown` filter is dropped rather than returning a page the user cannot recover from.
- The fallback's empty array also flows into `Search::Zoekt::Cache#search_fingerprint` (`ee/lib/search/zoekt/cache.rb:78-83`), where `known_languages.sort` is folded into the SHA256 digest alongside the query, scope, search mode, chunk size, and filters. A degraded search therefore hashes to a different cache key than a healthy one, so it cannot serve its filter-dropped results out of the cache to a later request that successfully built the language complement. No cache poisoning.
- This is deliberately not the approach rejected in the closed https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/251074. That one rescued inside `#fetch_language_tally`, which also swallowed the failure on the `aggregations` path and turned it into a 200 with empty buckets. This rescue sits in `#known_languages`, which is only on the search path. The `aggregations` action reaches the tally through `#language_aggregation_buckets`, not `#known_languages`, so it still returns 503 and the SLI still counts the failure.
- Raised by a GitLab Duo review comment on this MR: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254462#note_3808884067

What does not change:

- No user-visible change for the `aggregations` fix. `fetchAllAggregation` in `app/assets/javascripts/search/store/actions.js` (around lines 289-297) rejects on any non-2xx response and commits `RECEIVE_AGGREGATIONS_ERROR`, and `app/assets/javascripts/search/sidebar/components/language_filter/index.vue` renders the "Aggregations load error." alert. That was already true for the 500 and stays true for the 503.
- No new user-visible failure mode for the blob search fix either. Before it, an `Unknown`-filtered blob search with Zoekt down raised an unhandled exception; after it, the request returns the normal error result that `#zoekt_search` already produces for a downed backend, just without the `Unknown` filter applied.
- No change to SLI accounting on either path. `record_search_error` in `app/controllers/search_controller.rb` (around lines 172-181) flags an error when the status is 500 or above, so the `aggregations` failure is still counted, and it is reached through `#language_aggregation_buckets`, not through `#known_languages`.
- No changelog trailer for either commit: the language sidebar and its filters are behind the `zoekt_language_aggregations` feature flag (`ee/config/feature_flags/gitlab_com_derisk/zoekt_language_aggregations.yml`), which is `default_enabled: false`, and neither change is user-facing.

### Interaction with MR 254635

MR https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254635 moves the `Gitlab::Metrics::GlobalSearchSlis.record_error_rate` call in `BlobSearchResolver#results` out of the `if @search_results.failed?` branch into an `ensure`, so it records `error: @search_results.nil? || @search_results.server_error?` on every exit path. Combined with this MR, the GraphQL blob path with the `Unknown` language filter applied and a cold cache gets an outcome neither MR describes on its own:

| Tally request | Results request | Recorded by 254635 |
|---|---|---|
| fails | fails | `error: true` (unchanged in spirit) |
| fails | succeeds | `error: false` -- `known_languages` swallows the tally failure, results render with the `Unknown` filter silently dropped |

The second row is defensible: the user did get results. It's called out here so the outcome is a decision on record rather than an emergent property of merge order between the two MRs. There is no file-level conflict; the two MRs touch different files.

## References

- Earlier, closed attempt at the first fix: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/251074. It rescued inside `Search::Zoekt::SearchResults#fetch_language_tally` and returned an empty hash, turning the `aggregations` request into a 200 with empty buckets. That silently hid the Language section instead of showing the alert, and stopped the SLI from counting the failure. Closed in favour of the controller-level approach in this MR. The second commit here also touches `search_results.rb` but rescues in `#known_languages` instead, which does not affect the `aggregations` path; see the note under "Stop the language tally from failing the whole blob search" above.
- GitLab Duo review comment that raised the second issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254462#note_3808884067
- Feature flag rollout issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/605457
- Flag definition: `ee/config/feature_flags/gitlab_com_derisk/zoekt_language_aggregations.yml`

## Screenshots or screen recordings

No UI change. The "Aggregations load error." alert already rendered when the `aggregations` request failed with a 500; it renders the same way now that the request fails with a 503. The blob search page already has an error state for a downed Zoekt backend; the second commit only makes the `Unknown`-filtered case reach that same state instead of raising. No screenshots apply.

## How to set up and validate locally

1. Enable the flag in the rails console: `Feature.enable(:zoekt_language_aggregations)`
1. Make the Zoekt search endpoint unreachable, e.g. `gdk stop gitlab-zoekt-webserver-development-1 gitlab-zoekt-webserver-development-2`
1. Run an exact-code (blob) search in a Zoekt-indexed namespace.
1. Expect: results render, the sidebar shows "Aggregations load error.", and the request to `/search/aggregations` returns 503 with `{"error":"Search is currently unavailable. Please try again later.","error_type":"client_connection_error"}` instead of a 500.
1. Specs for the first commit: `bundle exec rspec ee/spec/controllers/ee/search_controller_spec.rb -e aggregations`, 24 examples, 0 failures. Two new examples cover the 503 body and that `record_error_rate` is still called with `error: true`; both fail if the rescue clause is removed.
1. With the flag still enabled and Zoekt still stopped, apply the `Unknown` language filter on a blob search. Before the second fix this raised an unhandled exception; after it, the blob search returns its normal error state and the `Unknown` filter is dropped instead.
1. Specs for the second commit: `bundle exec rspec ee/spec/lib/search/zoekt/search_results_spec.rb`, 137 examples, 0 failures. The new example was verified to fail without the rescue, with backtrace `fetch_language_tally` then `known_languages` then `zoekt_search_and_wrap` then `search_as_found_blob` then `blobs_and_file_count` then `objects`.

title: Add acquired_count and churned_count metric types
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Adds two metric types to the GitLab ClickHouse aggregation engine framework: `acquired_count`, which counts distinct values present in the current period but absent from the previous one (new users), and `churned_count`, which counts distinct values present in the previous period but absent from the current one.

The framework already provides `retained_count` (returning users) and `lagged_count` (previous-period users), added in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/627696. Without a server-side "new users" metric, dashboard consumers had to request two metrics and subtract them client-side to derive that number. With `acquired_count` and `churned_count` in place, the four metrics together give the full new/returning/churned picture from a single query, and churn rate becomes derivable from one response with no extra queries.

The implementation adds two new `BitmapWindow` operations, `:difference` and `:reverse_difference`, plus two thin metric classes modeled on the existing `RetainedCount`. Registering them in the engine's `metrics_mapping` exposes them through the DSL and GraphQL.

Both new operations apply `arrayDistinct` explicitly on each side before computing the set difference. `groupArray` keeps one element per underlying row, so a value with multiple rows in a period repeats in the array, while `arrayIntersect` (used by `retained_count`) dedupes implicitly, so that existing metric never needed this. This was verified empirically: removing `arrayDistinct` makes `acquired_count` return `2` instead of `1` for a period where one user has two rows, and six specs fail.

No engine declares either metric yet, so this MR has no user-facing behavior change. Wiring these metrics into the DuoWorkflows dashboard is a follow-up, out of scope for this issue.

## References

- Issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/628221
- Epic: https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/23225 (DAP Impact Dashboard v1)
- Prior related issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/627696 (added `retained_count` and `lagged_count`)

## Screenshots or screen recordings

Not applicable. This MR changes a backend aggregation framework only; there is no UI to capture.

## How to set up and validate locally

This change requires a local ClickHouse instance (available through GDK).

1. Run the specs for the new metric classes and the updated engine spec, tagged `click_house`:
   ```shell
   bundle exec rspec --tag click_house \
     spec/lib/gitlab/database/aggregation/click_house/acquired_count_spec.rb \
     spec/lib/gitlab/database/aggregation/click_house/churned_count_spec.rb \
     spec/lib/gitlab/database/aggregation/click_house/engine_spec.rb
   ```
   The `--tag click_house` flag is required, otherwise these examples are filtered out.
1. Run the updated `bitmap_window_spec.rb`. It is untagged, so it runs without the flag:
   ```shell
   bundle exec rspec spec/lib/gitlab/database/aggregation/click_house/bitmap_window_spec.rb
   ```

Locally observed results: 163 `click_house`-tagged examples and 415 untagged examples in `spec/lib/gitlab/database/aggregation` pass. RuboCop is clean. `markdownlint` and `vale` are clean on the updated doc.

It helps you analyze changes to reduce risks in quality, performance, reliability, security, and maintainability.

title: Add compacting indicator for Duo /compact command
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Duo Agentic Chat's `/compact` slash command asks the backend to summarise the conversation so it fits back into the model's context window. Until now the command gave no feedback while it ran: the user's literal `/compact` text sat in the transcript as an ordinary message bubble, and the only sign anything had happened arrived at the end, when the "Conversation compacted" divider rendered.

This replaces that bubble, while the command is in flight, with a pill-shaped row carrying a spinner and the label "Compacting…". Once anything follows the prompt in the message log, the prompt is dropped from the transcript entirely, so the finished state is just the divider.

### Not included, deliberately

No changelog entry and no new feature flag. Compaction is only reachable behind the existing default-off beta flag `ai_context_compaction`, and the indicator can only render when a user runs a command that flag gates. This matches the reasoning in the commit that added the compaction divider.

title: Add npm dist-tags Tags column to Artifact Registry version list
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

This MR renders a Tags column for npm versions in the Artifact Registry version list.

The column shows Artifact Registry (AR) per-version dist-tags. Container tags are not ready yet, so this MR covers only the npm half of the work.

Backend: `ArtifactRegistry::Version#dist_tags` reads the `dist_tags` key from the existing versions list response. It returns `[]` when the key is absent, null, or not an array. This adds no new AR request.

GraphQL: a new field `distTags: [String!]!` on `ArtifactRegistryVersion`. The field is marked experiment for milestone 19.4. GraphQL docs are regenerated.

Frontend (EE, behind the `artifact_registry_ui` feature flag): a Tags column appears after Version in the version list table. Each dist-tag renders as a `GlBadge` with variant `info`. A version with no tags shows muted text `untagged`.

The Tags column is a hideable optional column in the view-options popover Columns section. Maven gets neither the column nor the toggle, because Maven dist-tags are always `[]`.

A new helper, `versionsTableFields(format)`, drops the `tags` field for Maven in `utils.js`. The list fragment now selects `distTags`. The versions page still issues only its existing GraphQL queries, so this adds no extra network request.

With the `artifact_registry_ui` feature flag disabled, the versions connection resolves null before the client is called. This behavior is unchanged.

The container `tags` half waits on https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ops/artifact-registry/-/issues/1150 and is not in this MR.

## References

- Work item: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/628189 (Version list: render the Tags column from AR per-version dist-tags, monolith/S14 Phase 2)
- Epic: https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/epics/23331 (Version list, monolith/S14)
- AR contract issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ops/artifact-registry/-/issues/1153
- AR contract implementation: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ops/artifact-registry/-/merge_requests/2330 (in AR v2.19.0 and later)
- Container `tags` follow-up (not in this MR): https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ops/artifact-registry/-/issues/1150
- Row identity link styling, split into its own MR: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/254527

## Screenshots or screen recordings

| Before | After  |
| ------ | ------ |
| Phase 1 table had no Tags column (Version, Published, Source, Actions). | ![ar-tags-npm](/uploads/7a2dfa0fb23d365dd8d157a49e4158dd/ar-tags-npm.png) |
| View options popover had no Tags toggle. | ![ar-tags-toggle](/uploads/38bb464b73253798287bbf3c6d7ace23/ar-tags-toggle.png) |
| Maven package view had no Tags column, same as after. | ![ar-tags-maven](/uploads/c5b17ac1ba605f66e80fcb54e26d1b3e/ar-tags-maven.png) |

## How to set up and validate locally

1. Point your GitLab instance at an Artifact Registry at v2.19.0 or later.
1. In the Rails console, run `Feature.enable(:artifact_registry_ui)`.
1. Activate an organization for Artifact Registry with an npm hosted repository that has a published package.
1. Run `npm dist-tag add <pkg>@<version> next` to add a second tag to a version.
1. Open the organization Artifact Registry repositories page, then the npm repository, then the package.
1. Check that the Tags column shows the dist-tags as `GlBadge` items, and `untagged` for versions with no tags.
1. Open the view options popover and toggle the Tags column on and off.
1. Open a Maven package and confirm it has no Tags column and no Tags toggle.
1. Optionally, run this GraphQL query to confirm the field directly:

   ```graphql
   organization {
     artifactRegistryRepository(name: "...") {
       packages {
         nodes {
           ... on ArtifactRegistryNpmPackage {
             versions {
               nodes {
                 version
                 distTags
               }
             }
           }
         }
       }
     }
   ```

title: Add created_by_duo marker to MergeRequests analytics
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Adds a `created_by_duo` flag to the ClickHouse merge request analytics data, so it's possible to tell which MRs were created through a GitLab Duo Agent Platform (DAP) session. This is needed for the DAP Impact Dashboard, which wants to show an "Agent MR acceptance rate": the share of Duo-created MRs that end up merged. The aggregation engine also gains a general `acceptanceRate` metric and a `createdByDuo` dimension/filter, exposed over GraphQL.

Changes:

- ClickHouse schema: new `created_by_duo` column on the `merge_requests` analytics table, sourced from the `siphon_duo_workflows_workflow_merge_requests` link table (only `created` links, deduplicated, soft-deleted rows excluded).
- Materialized view: `merge_requests_mv` is updated in place (`ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY QUERY`) so it keeps populating the flag on new and re-replicated MR rows, with no gap in inserts. A projection on the link table keyed by `merge_request_id` keeps the lookup efficient.
- Backfill: a post-deploy migration sets `created_by_duo = true` for existing MRs that already have a `created` link. It runs as an async mutation and is idempotent.
- Aggregation engine / GraphQL: new `createdByDuo` dimension and filter, and a new `acceptanceRate` metric, available through `analytics.mergeRequests`.

Notes:

- The flag is set when an MR row is created or re-replicated, so it lands on creation or the next update; the backfill covers MRs that already existed.
- Only MRs created through a DAP session after the `created` link was introduced will carry the flag.

## References

- Issue: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/608191
- DAP Impact Dashboard epic: https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/23225
- Depends on #616992 (Siphon replication of the link table)

## Screenshots or screen recordings

Backend and ClickHouse schema changes only, no UI changes.

## How to set up and validate locally

1. Run ClickHouse migrations: `bundle exec rake gitlab:clickhouse:migrate`
2. Insert a `created` link row for an existing MR into `siphon_duo_workflows_workflow_merge_requests` (link_type = 1) via the ClickHouse client, or create an MR through a Duo Agent Platform session.
3. Re-insert / re-replicate the MR row into `siphon_merge_requests` (or run the backfill migration) so the materialized view picks it up, then check `SELECT id, created_by_duo FROM merge_requests FINAL WHERE id = <mr_id>` returns true.
4. Query GraphQL, e.g.:
```graphql
query {
  group(fullPath: "<group-path>") {
    analytics {
      mergeRequests(createdByDuo: [true]) {
        aggregated {
          nodes {
            dimensions { createdByDuo }
            acceptanceRate
            throughputCount
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```
5. Run specs:
```shell
bundle exec rspec ee/spec/models/analytics/aggregation_engines/merge_requests_spec.rb \
  ee/spec/requests/api/graphql/analytics/merge_requests_spec.rb \
  spec/db/click_house/post_migrate/20260910104402_backfill_created_by_duo_on_merge_requests_spec.rb
```
